Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 10, verses 1–2:

It is a Meccan surah.

{1} The Exalted says: {Alif, Lam, Ra. These are the verses of the Wise Book}: that is, this Qur'an, which comprises wisdom and rulings, whose verses point to the matters of faith and to the legislated commands and prohibitions, and which all of the Ummah must receive with contentment, acceptance and submission.

{2} Yet despite this, most of them turned away, for they do not know. So they marvelled {that We revealed to a man from among them: "Warn the people"}: of God's punishment, warn them of God's vengeance, and remind them of God's signs, {"and give good tidings to those who have believed"}: with true faith {"that they will have a sure standing [qadam sidq] with their Lord"}; that is, they will have a full reward and a stored-up recompense with their Lord for the righteous and sincere good deeds they have sent ahead and done beforehand. The disbelievers marvelled at this great man in a manner that led them to disbelieve in him! So {the disbelievers said} of him: {"Indeed, this is a clear magician"}; that is, plainly a sorcerer, which in their assumption is hidden from no one. This was from their foolishness and obstinacy. They marvelled at a matter that is not worthy of marvel or astonishment; rather, what deserves marvel is their ignorance and their failure to know their own interests. How did they not believe in this noble Messenger whom God raised up from among themselves, whom they know in the truest sense of knowing? Instead they rejected his call and were eager to nullify his religion! But God will complete His light, though the disbelievers dislike it.

{3} He, exalted, says, explaining His lordship, His divinity, and His greatness: ﴿Indeed, your Lord is Allah, who created the heavens and the earth in six days﴾. Although He is able to create them in a single instant, He did so for a divine wisdom He has, and because He is gentle (rafiq) in His actions. Among His wisdom in it is that He created them with truth and for truth, so that He may be known by His names and attributes, and be singled out for worship. ﴿Then﴾, after creating the heavens and the earth, ﴿He established Himself upon the Throne﴾ (al-'Arsh), an establishment befitting His greatness. ﴿He arranges the affair﴾ in the upper and lower world: giving death and life, sending down provisions, alternating the days among people, removing harm from those in distress, and answering the requests of those who ask. All kinds of arrangement descend from Him and ascend to Him, and all creation submits to His might and is humbled before His greatness and authority. ﴿There is no intercessor except after His permission﴾. So none of them ventures to intercede, even if he were the best of creation, until Allah gives permission. He gives permission only to whom He is pleased with, and He is pleased only with the people of sincerity and monotheism toward Him. ﴿That is Allah, your Lord﴾; i.e., He is the Allah who possesses the attribute of divinity, which encompasses all the attributes of perfection, and the attribute of lordship, which encompasses the attributes of action. ﴿So worship Him﴾; i.e., single Him out with all the kinds of worship you are able to perform. ﴿Will you not remember?﴾ That is, the evidences indicating that He alone is the one worthy of worship, the praised, the Possessor of majesty and honor.

{4} When He mentioned His decreed judgment, which is the general arrangement, and His religious judgment, which is His law whose content and purpose is worshipping Him alone without partner, He mentioned the judgment of recompense, which is His requiting deeds after death, saying: ﴿To Him is your return, all of you﴾; i.e., He will gather you after your death for the appointed time of a known day. ﴿Indeed, He originates creation, then repeats it﴾. The One able to originate creation is able to repeat it. Whoever sees its origination and then denies its repetition lacks sound reason, for he denies one of two like things while affirming what is more fitting than it. So this is a clear rational proof for the Return. Then he mentioned the transmitted proof, saying: ﴿The promise of Allah is true﴾; i.e., His promise is truthful and must be fulfilled. ﴿That He may reward those who believe﴾ with their hearts, in what Allah commanded them to believe, ﴿and do righteous deeds﴾ with their limbs, of obligations and recommended acts, ﴿with justice﴾; i.e., by their faith and their deeds, a reward He has made clear to His servants, informing them that no soul knows what has been hidden for them of comfort for the eyes. ﴿And those who disbelieved﴾ in the signs of Allah and denied the messengers of Allah, ﴿for them is a drink of scalding water﴾; i.e., hot water that scalds the faces and cuts the intestines, ﴿and a painful punishment﴾ of all the kinds of punishment, ﴿because they used to disbelieve﴾; i.e., because of their disbelief and wrongdoing. Allah did not wrong them, but they were wronging themselves.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 10, verses 5–6:

{5–6} When he had established His lordship and His divinity, he mentioned the rational, horizontal proofs that indicate this and indicate His perfection in His names and attributes: the sun, the moon, the heavens and the earth, and all that He created in them of the various kinds of creatures. He informed us that they are signs ﴿for a people who know﴾ and ﴿for a people who fear God﴾, for knowledge guides one to recognizing the indication within them and how to derive the proofs in the closest manner, while piety (taqwa) produces in the heart a desire for good and a dread of evil, arising from the evidences and proofs and from knowledge and certainty.

The sum of this is that the mere creation of these creatures in this manner indicates the perfection of God's power, knowledge, life and self-subsistence (qayyumiyyah). The precision, perfection, originality and beauty within them indicate the perfection of God's wisdom, the excellence of His creation and the breadth of His knowledge. The various kinds of benefits and interests within them, such as His making the sun a radiance and the moon a light, through which arises the necessary benefit and other benefits that arise, indicate God's mercy, His care for His servants, and the vastness of His kindness and beneficence. The specifications found within them indicate God's will and His executing purpose, and this indicates that He alone is the one worshipped, the one loved, the one praised, possessor of majesty, honor and great attributes, to whom alone desire and dread are due, and to whom alone pure supplication is directed, not to any other of the created, sustained beings who are in need of God in all their affairs.

In these verses there is an exhortation and encouragement to reflect upon God's creatures and to consider them with the eye of contemplation, for by this insight is widened, faith and intellect increase, and the mind's faculty of discernment grows strong. Neglecting this is a slackness regarding what God has commanded, a closing of the door to increase in faith, and a stagnation of the mind and its faculty.

{7} The Exalted says: ﴿Indeed, those who do not expect to meet Us﴾; that is, they do not hope for the meeting with Allah, which is the greatest thing that those who hope aspire to and the highest thing that the faithful aspire to. Rather, they turn away from that, and at times they deny it. ﴿And they are content with the worldly life﴾ instead of the Hereafter, ﴿and they are at rest in it﴾; that is, they lean upon it and make it the ultimate goal of their affairs and the final aim of their intentions. So they strive for it and devote themselves to its pleasures and desires, by whatever means it is attained, and from whatever direction it appears they hasten to it. They have directed their wills, intentions, thoughts and actions toward it, as if they were created to remain in it, and as if it were not a place of passage where travelers take provision for the lasting abode to which the first and the last will journey, and toward whose bliss and delights the successful ones strive. ﴿And those who are heedless of Our signs﴾: they do not benefit from the Qur'anic signs, nor from the signs in the horizons and in themselves; and turning away from the proof necessarily entails turning away from and heedlessness of the intended meaning it indicates.

{8} ﴿Those﴾: those whose description is this, ﴿their abode is the Fire﴾; that is, their place of settlement and dwelling from which they will never depart; ﴿because of what they used to earn﴾: of disbelief, associating partners with Allah, and various kinds of sins.

Having mentioned their punishment, he then mentioned the reward of the obedient, saying:

Having mentioned their punishment, he then mentioned the reward of the obedient, saying:

{9} He says, exalted is He: "Indeed, those who believed and did righteous deeds" — that is, they combined faith with fulfilling its requirements and its consequences of righteous deeds, comprising deeds of the heart and deeds of the limbs, with sincerity and following (of the Prophet's way). "Their Lord guides them by their faith" — that is, because of the faith they have, Allah rewards them with the greatest reward, which is guidance. He teaches them what benefits them, bestows upon them deeds arising from that guidance, guides them to reflect upon His signs, guides them in this world to the straight path, and in the straight path, and in the abode of recompense to the path that leads to the Gardens of bliss. For this reason He said: "Rivers flow beneath them" — flowing continuously. "In Gardens of bliss" — Allah attributed them to bliss because they encompass complete bliss: the bliss of the heart through joy, delight, happiness and gladness, seeing the All-Merciful and hearing His speech, rejoicing in His good pleasure and nearness, meeting beloved ones and brothers, enjoying gathering with them, hearing enchanting voices, moving melodies and delightful sights; and the bliss of the body through various kinds of food, drink, spouses and the like, of what no soul knows and which has not occurred to anyone's mind, or which describers could not describe.

{10} "Their prayer therein is: 'Glory be to You, O Allah'" — that is, their worship therein to Allah; at its beginning is glorifying Allah and declaring Him free from imperfections, and at its end is praising Allah. The obligations have dropped from them in the abode of recompense, and there remains for them only the most perfect of pleasures, which is more delightful to them than delicious foods, namely the remembrance of Allah, by which hearts are reassured and spirits rejoice, and which is for them like breath to the self, without exertion or hardship. "And" as for their greeting among themselves when they meet and visit one another, it is "peace" — that is, speech free from idle talk and sin, described as "peace." It has been said in explanation of His words: "Their prayer therein is: 'Glory be to You, [O Allah]...'" to the end of the verse: when the people of Paradise need food, drink and the like, they say: "Glory be to You, O Allah!" and it is brought to them immediately; and when they finish, they say: "Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds."

This is one of the kindnesses and favours of Allah towards His servants: if He hastened evil upon them whenever they brought about its causes, and immediately punished them for that, just as He hastens good for them when they bring about its causes, {the term would have been decreed for them}; that is, the punishment would have destroyed them. But Allah, exalted is He, gives them respite and does not neglect them, and He pardons much of what is due to Him. Were Allah to take people to task for their wrongdoing, He would not leave upon its back a single creature. Included in this is that when a servant grows angry at his children, his family, or his wealth, he may sometimes utter a supplication against them which, if it were accepted from him, would destroy them, and it would harm him in the greatest degree. But Allah is Most Forbearing, Most Wise.

As for His words, {So We leave those who do not expect the meeting with Us}: that is, those who do not believe in the Hereafter, and therefore do not prepare for it, nor do they do what would save them from the punishment of Allah. {In their transgression}: that is, in their falsehood by which they have exceeded the truth and its limits. {Wandering blindly}: they wander bewildered, not finding the way, and are not guided to the straightest proof. This is a punishment for them for their wrongdoing and their disbelief in the signs of Allah.

This is an information about the nature of man as such: that when harm touches him, whether illness or calamity, he strives in supplication and asks God in all his conditions, standing, sitting, and lying on his side, and he persists in supplication so that God may remove his harm. ﴿But when We remove his harm from him, he passes on as if he had never invoked Us against a harm that touched him﴾; i.e., he continues in his heedlessness, turning away from his Lord, as if no harm had come to him which God removed from him. What injustice is greater than this injustice? He asks God to fulfil his need, and when He grants it to him, he does not regard the right of his Lord, as though he owes God no right at all! This is an embellishment from Satan, who made appealing to him what is repugnant and abhorrent to intellects and natural dispositions. ﴿Thus has it been made appealing to the wasteful﴾; i.e., those who transgress the limit, ﴿what they used to do﴾.

{13} He, may He be exalted, informs that He destroyed the earlier nations for their wrongdoing and disbelief, after clear signs had come to them through the messengers, making the truth plain. Yet they did not submit to them, nor did they believe. So He brought upon them His punishment, which is not turned back from every criminal who is bold toward the sacred prohibitions of Allah. This is His way (sunnah) with all nations.

{14} {Then We made you} — O you who are addressed — {successors (khala'if) in the earth after them, that We may see how you will act}. So if you take heed, are admonished by those before you, follow the signs of Allah, and believe His messengers, you will be saved in this world and the Hereafter. But if you act as the wrongdoers before you acted, He will bring upon you what He brought upon them. And whoever has been warned has been given an excuse (fa-qad a'dhara).

{15} Almighty God mentions the obstinacy of those who denied His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ), and that when the Qur'anic verses of God that make the truth clear are recited to them, they turn away from them and seek forms of obstinacy. Out of audacity and wrongdoing they said: {Bring a Qur'an other than this, or change it.} May God condemn them! How audacious they are toward God, and how great their wrongdoing and their rejection of His verses! If the Great Messenger is commanded by God to say to them: {Say: It is not for me} — that is, it is not fitting or proper — {to change it on my own accord;} for I am only a pure messenger, and I have no share in the matter at all. {I follow only what is revealed to me} — that is, I have nothing other than that; I am a servant who is commanded. {Indeed, I fear, if I disobey my Lord, the punishment of a tremendous Day.} This is the word of the best of creation and his good conduct toward the commands of his Lord and His revelation. How then can it be with these foolish, misguided people who have combined ignorance, error, wrongdoing, stubbornness, obstinacy and the challenging of the Lord of the worlds? Do they not fear the punishment of a tremendous Day? If they claim that their intention is for the truth to become clear to them through the signs they have requested, they are liars in that claim, for God has already shown among the signs what humankind can be made to believe by their like, and He is the One who directs them as He wills, in accordance with His lordly wisdom and His mercy toward His servants.

{16} {Say: Had God willed, I would not have recited it to you, nor would He have made you aware of it. I have dwelt among you a lifetime} — a long time — {before it}; that is, before its recitation and before your knowledge of it, and it never occurred to me nor entered my thoughts. {Will you not then reason?} That since I did not fabricate it during the span of my life, and nothing proceeded from me that indicates it, how could I fabricate it afterwards, when I have dwelt among you a long time, and you know the reality of my condition: that I am an unlettered man who does not read, does not write, does not study, and does not learn from anyone? Then I bring you a tremendous Book that overwhelms the eloquent and baffles the scholars. Is it possible, with this, that it comes from my own self? Or is this not a decisive proof that it is a revelation from the All-Wise, the Praiseworthy? So if you were to apply your thoughts and minds, and reflect upon my condition and the condition of this Book, you would be certain beyond any doubt of its truth, and that it is the truth beyond which there is only error. But if you insist upon denial and obstinacy, then undoubtedly you are wrongdoers.

{17} And {Who is more unjust than one who fabricates a lie against God or denies His signs?} For if I were a fabricator, I would be the most unjust of people, and I would have lost success, and my condition would not have been hidden from you. But I have brought you the signs of God, and you denied them; thus wrongdoing is established in you, and your affair will certainly perish, and you will not attain success as long as you remain so. His saying {Those who do not expect to meet Us say...} indicates — the verse — that what drove them to this obstinacy that proceeded from them is their lack of belief in meeting God and their lack of hope for it; and whoever believes in meeting God must submit to this Book and believe in it, because it is of sound intention.

But I have brought you the signs of God, and you denied them; thus wrongdoing is established in you, and your affair will certainly perish, and you will not attain success as long as you remain so. His saying {Those who do not expect to meet Us say...} indicates — the verse — that what drove them to this obstinacy that proceeded from them is their lack of belief in meeting God and their lack of hope for it; and whoever believes in meeting God must submit to this Book and believe in it, because it is of sound intention.

{15} Almighty God mentions the obstinacy of those who denied His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ), and that when the Qur'anic verses of God that make the truth clear are recited to them, they turn away from them and seek forms of obstinacy. Out of audacity and wrongdoing they said: {Bring a Qur'an other than this, or change it.} May God condemn them! How audacious they are toward God, and how great their wrongdoing and their rejection of His verses! If the Great Messenger is commanded by God to say to them: {Say: It is not for me} — that is, it is not fitting or proper — {to change it on my own accord;} for I am only a pure messenger, and I have no share in the matter at all. {I follow only what is revealed to me} — that is, I have nothing other than that; I am a servant who is commanded. {Indeed, I fear, if I disobey my Lord, the punishment of a tremendous Day.} This is the word of the best of creation and his good conduct toward the commands of his Lord and His revelation. How then can it be with these foolish, misguided people who have combined ignorance, error, wrongdoing, stubbornness, obstinacy and the challenging of the Lord of the worlds? Do they not fear the punishment of a tremendous Day? If they claim that their intention is for the truth to become clear to them through the signs they have requested, they are liars in that claim, for God has already shown among the signs what humankind can be made to believe by their like, and He is the One who directs them as He wills, in accordance with His lordly wisdom and His mercy toward His servants.

{16} {Say: Had God willed, I would not have recited it to you, nor would He have made you aware of it. I have dwelt among you a lifetime} — a long time — {before it}; that is, before its recitation and before your knowledge of it, and it never occurred to me nor entered my thoughts. {Will you not then reason?} That since I did not fabricate it during the span of my life, and nothing proceeded from me that indicates it, how could I fabricate it afterwards, when I have dwelt among you a long time, and you know the reality of my condition: that I am an unlettered man who does not read, does not write, does not study, and does not learn from anyone? Then I bring you a tremendous Book that overwhelms the eloquent and baffles the scholars. Is it possible, with this, that it comes from my own self? Or is this not a decisive proof that it is a revelation from the All-Wise, the Praiseworthy? So if you were to apply your thoughts and minds, and reflect upon my condition and the condition of this Book, you would be certain beyond any doubt of its truth, and that it is the truth beyond which there is only error. But if you insist upon denial and obstinacy, then undoubtedly you are wrongdoers.

{17} And {Who is more unjust than one who fabricates a lie against God or denies His signs?} For if I were a fabricator, I would be the most unjust of people, and I would have lost success, and my condition would not have been hidden from you. But I have brought you the signs of God, and you denied them; thus wrongdoing is established in you, and your affair will certainly perish, and you will not attain success as long as you remain so. His saying {Those who do not expect to meet Us say...} indicates — the verse — that what drove them to this obstinacy that proceeded from them is their lack of belief in meeting God and their lack of hope for it; and whoever believes in meeting God must submit to this Book and believe in it, because it is of sound intention.

{18} The Exalted says: {And they worship} — that is, the polytheists who denied the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) — {besides Allah what neither harms them nor benefits them} — that is, it possesses not the weight of an atom's worth of benefit for them, nor does it repel anything from them. {And they say}, a statement devoid of proof: {These are our intercessors with Allah} — that is, they worship them so that they may bring them near to Allah and intercede for them with Him. This is a saying of their own invention, a speech they originated themselves. For this reason He said, refuting this claim: {Say, "Will you inform Allah of what He does not know in the heavens or on the earth?"} — that is, Allah, exalted is He, is the All-Knowing who encompasses in knowledge everything in the heavens and the earth, and He has informed you that He has no partner and no god besides Him. Yet you, O company of polytheists, claim that He has partners within them. Will you inform Him of a matter hidden from Him, which you have come to know? Are you more knowing than Allah? Is there any statement more false than this one, which implies that these misguided, ignorant, foolish people are more knowing than the Lord of the worlds? Let the intelligent person be content with merely conceiving this statement, for he will be certain of its corruption and falsehood. {Exalted is He above what they associate} — that is, He is sanctified and far removed from having a partner or equal. Rather, He is Allah, the One, the Unique, the Eternal Refuge, besides whom there is no god in the heavens and the earth, and every object of worship in the higher and lower worlds other than Him is false by reason, by revealed law, and by innate nature. {That is because Allah is the Truth, and what they invoke besides Him is the falsehood, and because Allah is the Most High, the Great}.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 10, verse 19–20:

{19} That is: ﴿And mankind was not but one community﴾, agreed upon the correct religion; but they differed. ﴿So Allah sent the messengers as bringers of good tidings and warners, and sent down with them the Book in truth to judge between the people concerning that over which they differed﴾. ﴿And if not for a word that had preceded from your Lord﴾: [that is,] the delaying of the disobedient and not hastening to punish them for their sins, ﴿it would have been decided between them﴾: by saving the believers and destroying the disbelieving deniers, and this would have become the distinction between them ﴿concerning that over which they differ﴾. But He willed to test them and to try some of them by means of others, so that the truthful might be distinguished from the liar.

{20} ﴿And they say﴾; i.e., the deniers who are obstinate: ﴿Why has a sign not been sent down to him from his Lord?﴾; meaning: the signs of their own suggestion which they specify, like their saying: ﴿Why has an angel not been sent down to him so that he would be a warner with him?﴾ ... [to the end of the verses], and like their saying: ﴿And they say, "We will not believe you until you cause to gush forth for us from the earth a spring"﴾ ... [to the end of the verses]. ﴿So say﴾: to them, when they ask you for a sign: ﴿The unseen belongs only to Allah﴾; i.e., He is the one who encompasses the states of the servants in knowledge, so He manages them by what His knowledge concerning them requires and His wondrous wisdom, and no one has any management in a judgment, nor any proof, nor any purpose, nor any reason. ﴿So wait; indeed, I am with you among the waiting﴾; i.e., each one awaits with his companion what he deserves, so look to see whose will be the final outcome.

{21} Almighty God says: {And when We let people taste mercy after some hardship has touched them}: such as health after sickness, wealth after poverty, and security after fear. {They forget what hardship befell them, and do not thank God for the ease and mercy; rather, they persist in their rebellion and their deceit.} For this reason He says: {Indeed, they have scheming against Our signs}; that is, they strive in falsehood to nullify the truth thereby. {Say: God is swifter in scheming.} Indeed, evil scheming does not befall anyone except its own people; so their intention is reversed upon them, and they are not spared the consequence. Rather, the angels record what they do, and God counts it against them, and then God recompenses them for it with the fullest recompense.

{22–23} When Allah, exalted is He, mentioned the general principle concerning people's states when mercy reaches them after hardship, and ease after difficulty, He mentioned a situation that confirms this, namely their state at sea when it becomes rough and they fear its consequences. He said:

﴿It is He who enables you to travel on land and sea.﴾ By the means He has made easy for you to travel in them, and He guided you to them.

﴿Until, when you are in the ships and they sail with them by a good wind,﴾ i.e., the sea-going vessels, ﴿and they rejoice in it,﴾ that is, they are reassured by it. ﴿Then a violent wind comes upon them, and the waves come at them from every place, and they think they are encompassed.﴾ That is, they realize it is destruction. At that point their attachment to created beings ends, and they know that nothing will save them from this calamity except Allah alone, so they call upon Him, ﴿sincere in religion to Him,﴾ and they pledge on themselves in an obligatory manner, saying: ﴿If You save us from this, we will surely be among the grateful.﴾ ﴿But when He has saved them, immediately they commit injustice in the earth without right.﴾ That is, they forgot that hardship, that supplication, and what they had obligated themselves to, so they associated with Allah those whom they had acknowledged cannot save them from hardships nor repel their distress. Why did they not devote worship sincerely to Allah in ease as they did in hardship? But this transgression returns its harm upon them, and for this He said:

﴿O mankind, your transgression is only against yourselves—the enjoyment of worldly life.﴾ That is, the furthest aim you seek through your transgression and your deviation from sincerity to Allah is to obtain some of the trifling, meager wealth and status of this world, which will soon end and all pass away, and then you will leave it against your will.

﴿Then to Us is your return,﴾ on the Day of Resurrection, ﴿and We will inform you of what you used to do.﴾ In this is the utmost warning to them against persisting in their deeds.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 10, verse 24:

{24} This parable is among the finest of parables, and it corresponds exactly to the state of this world. Its pleasures, its desires, its status and the like flaunt themselves to their possessor for a brief time if they flourish; but when they reach completion and perfection, they wither away and vanish from their possessor, or he vanishes from them, so that he becomes empty-handed of them, his heart filled with their worry, their sorrow and their regret. This is ﴿like water which We send down from the sky, and with it the plants of the earth mingle﴾; i.e., there grew in it every kind and a delightful pair, ﴿of that which men eat﴾, such as grains and fruits, ﴿and cattle﴾ [also eat], such as various kinds of herbage and pasture of differing types. ﴿Until, when the earth takes on its adornment and becomes beautiful﴾; i.e., it adorned itself in its appearance and clothed itself in its finery, so that it became a delight to onlookers, a pleasure to spectators, and a sign for those who reflect, so that you see for it a wondrous appearance, between green, yellow, white and other colors. ﴿And its people think that they have power over it﴾; i.e., there arose in them a hope that this would continue and endure, because their wills had come to rest upon it and their aims in it had been fulfilled. But while they were in that state, there came upon it the command of Allah, ﴿by night or by day, and We made it a harvested stubble, as though it had not flourished yesterday﴾; i.e., as though it had never been. Such is the state of this world, exactly alike. ﴿Thus do We detail the signs﴾; i.e., We make them clear and explain them by bringing meanings close to minds and by coining parables, ﴿for a people who reflect﴾; i.e., who employ their thoughts in what benefits them. As for the heedless and the averse, these signs do not benefit them, and clarification does not remove their doubt.

When Allah mentioned the state of this world and the sum of its bounties, He stirred longing for the everlasting abode, saying:

{25} The Exalted has made a general call to His servants to come to the Abode of Peace (dar al-salam), urging them toward it and encouraging them. He singles out for guidance whomever He wills to choose and elect. This is His grace and His kindness; "Allah singles out for His mercy whomever He wills" (Qur'an 2:105). That is His justice and His wisdom, and no one has any proof against Him after the clarification and the messengers. Allah named Paradise the Abode of Peace because it is safe from all afflictions and deficiencies, and that is due to the perfection of its bliss, its completeness, its permanence, and its beauty in every respect.

{26} When He called to the Abode of Peace, it was as if souls yearned for the deeds that necessitate it and lead to it, so He informed about them with His saying: {For those who do good is the best (al-husna) and more} (Qur'an 10:26). That is: for those who do good in the worship of the Creator, by worshipping Him with the awareness of His presence (muraqabah) and sincere counsel (nasihah) in their servitude, and by fulfilling what they are able of it; and who do good to Allah's servants, by what they are able of good in speech and action: by giving of their wealth, by bodily kindness, by enjoining what is good and forbidding what is evil, by teaching the ignorant, by advising those who turn away, and other forms of righteousness and goodness. For these, the "best" is theirs, which is the complete Paradise in its beauty, "and more," which is gazing upon the Noble Face of Allah, hearing His speech, attaining His good pleasure, and the joy of His nearness. Through this they obtain the highest of what the wishers wish for and what those who ask request.

Then He mentioned the removal of what is feared for them, saying: {And neither dust nor humiliation shall cover their faces} (Qur'an 10:26); that is, no harm shall reach them in any way, because when something disliked befalls a person, it shows on his face: it changes and becomes troubled. As for these, as Allah said of them: {You recognize in their faces the radiance of bliss} (Qur'an 83:24). "They are the companions of the Garden, abiding therein eternally" (Qur'an 2:82), who do not shift, do not depart, and do not change.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 10, verse 27:

{27} When He mentioned the People of the Garden, He mentioned the People of the Fire. He stated that their merchandise, which they acquired in the world, consists of evil deeds that anger Allah, of various kinds of disbelief and denial and types of sins. So their recompense is an evil like it; that is, a recompense that distresses them according to the evil deeds they committed in their various states. {And humiliation will cover them}; that is, it will overwhelm them: humiliation in their hearts and fear of the punishment of Allah, which no one can repel from them and no protector can shield them from. That inner humiliation will spread to their outward appearance, so it will become blackness in their faces. {As if their faces were covered with pieces of the dark night. Those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein eternally}: How great is the difference between the two groups! How far apart is the disparity between them! {Faces that Day will be radiant, looking toward their Lord} {And faces that Day will be gloomy, expecting that a calamity will be done to them} {Faces that Day will be bright, laughing and joyful. And faces that Day will have dust upon them, overcast with darkness. Those are the disbelievers, the wicked.}

{28} He, the Exalted, says: {And on the Day We shall gather them all together}; that is, We shall assemble all creatures for the appointed time of a known day, and We shall bring the polytheists and those they used to worship besides Allah. {Then We shall say to those who associated partners: Stay in your place, you and your partners}; that is, remain in your places so that judgment and separation may take place between you and them. {Then We shall separate them}; that is, We shall divide them by physical and spiritual distance, so that intense enmity arises between them after they had offered them in the world pure love and sincere affection. That love and loyalty turn into hatred and hostility. {And their partners will disown them and say: You did not worship us}; for we exalt Allah above having any partner or equal.

{29} {Allah suffices as a witness between us and you that we were indeed unaware of your worship}: We did not command you to it, nor did we call you to it. Rather, you worshipped the one who called you to it, and that is Satan; as Allah the Exalted says: {Did I not enjoin upon you, O children of Adam, that you should not worship Satan? Indeed, he is to you a clear enemy}. And He says: {And on the Day He will gather them all and say to the angels, "Did these used to worship you?" They will say, "Exalted are You; You are our Protector, not them. Rather, they used to worship the jinn; most of them were believers in them."} So the noble angels, the prophets, the saints and their likes will disown those who worshipped them on the Day of Resurrection, and will disassociate themselves from their calling them to worship. They are the truthful and righteous in this.

{30} Then the polytheists will be seized with an indescribable regret, and they will know the measure of the deeds they sent forward and the evil traits they had earlier committed. It will become clear to them on that day that they were liars and that they had fabricated against Allah. Their worship will have gone astray, their objects of worship will have vanished, and the means and causes will have been cut off from them. Therefore He said: {There, every soul will test what it has sent forward}; that is, on that day it will examine its deeds and earnings and be recompensed accordingly: if good, then good, and if evil, then evil. {And they will lose what they used to fabricate}: from their claim of the soundness of what they held of polytheism, and that what they worshipped besides Allah would benefit them and ward off punishment from them.

{31} That is: say to these people who associated partners with God, without any authority from Him, arguing against them with what they acknowledged of Tawhid al-Rububiyyah (the oneness of Lordship) in order to refute what they denied of Tawhid al-Uluhiyyah (the oneness of divinity): {Say: "Who provides for you from the heaven and the earth?"} By sending down provision from the sky, bringing forth its varieties from the earth, and facilitating its causes within it. {Or who controls hearing and sight?} That is: who created them and who owns them? They are singled out for mention as a way of drawing attention to the lesser by means of the greater, and because of their great honour and benefit. {And who brings the living out of the dead} like bringing forth varieties of trees and plants from grains and date-pits, bringing the believer out of the disbeliever, the bird out of the egg... and the like. {And brings the dead out of the living}: the reverse of what has been mentioned. {And who governs the affair} in the upper and lower worlds, and this encompasses all kinds of divine governance. For when you ask them about this, {they will say, "God."} because they acknowledge all of that, and that God has no partner in any of what has been mentioned. {So say} to them, as a binding argument: {"Will you not then fear Him?"} God, so that you single Him out in worship, alone, without partner, and abandon what you worship besides Him of rivals and idols.

{32} {Then that is God, your Lord}: the One who described Himself with what He described Himself with; that is, the One worthy of worship, the one who is praised, who nurtures all creation with blessings. {So what is there after the truth but error?} For He, exalted is He, is the One alone who creates and governs all things, the One from whom every blessing the servants have comes, who alone brings good deeds and alone repels evil deeds, possessor of the Most Beautiful Names, the great perfect attributes, majesty and honour. {How then are you turned away?} From worshipping One with such attributes to worshipping one who has from his existence nothing but non-existence, who possesses for himself no benefit, no harm, no death, no life, and no resurrection; he has not even an atom's weight of dominion, and has no share in any way, and intercedes with God only by His permission.

{33} So woe to those who associate others with Him, and doom to those who disbelieve in Him. They have lost their minds after they lost their religion; indeed they have lost both their worldly life and their hereafter. For this reason God, exalted is He, said about them: {Thus the word of your Lord has come true against those who defiantly disobeyed, that they will not believe.} after God had shown them clear signs and luminous proofs, which contain a lesson for people of understanding, an admonition for the God-fearing, and guidance for all the worlds.

{34} Almighty God says, clarifying the impotence of the idols of the polytheists and that they lack the attributes that would warrant taking them as gods besides God: ﴿Say: "Is there any of your partners who originates creation and then repeats it?"﴾ That is, who begins it. This is a rhetorical question carrying the meaning of negation and affirmation: none of them originates creation and then repeats it. They are weaker than that and more incapable. ﴿Say: "God originates creation and then repeats it"﴾ without any partner or helper in that. ﴿So how are you deluded?﴾ That is, you are turned away and diverted from worshipping the One who alone originates and repeats creation, toward worshipping one who creates nothing, while they themselves are created.

{35} ﴿Say: "Is there any of your partners who guides to the truth?"﴾ By explaining it and guiding to it, or by inspiring it and granting success. ﴿Say: "God"﴾ alone ﴿guides to the truth﴾ through proofs and demonstrations, and through inspiration, success, and help in following the most upright path. ﴿Is He who guides, or one who cannot find guidance unless he is guided?﴾ That is, one who cannot be guided unless he is guided, due to his lack of knowledge and his misguidance. These are their partners, which neither guide nor are guided unless they are guided. ﴿What is the matter with you? How do you judge?﴾ That is, what made you pass this false judgment, that the worship of anyone besides God is valid, after the proof and the evidence have become manifest that none deserves worship but God alone? If it becomes clear that their gods, whom they worship besides God, possess neither inherent attributes nor active attributes that necessitate their being worshipped besides God, but rather are characterized by deficiencies that void their divinity, then for what reason were they made gods besides God?

{36} The answer: this is among the adornments of Satan to humanity, the most ugly falsehood and the most misguided error, until one believes it, becomes accustomed to it, and thinks it true, when it is nothing. For this reason He says: ﴿And those who call upon other than God as partners do not actually follow partners of God﴾ That is, in reality they do not follow partners of God, for God has no partner at all, by reason or by transmitted textual evidence. They only follow conjecture, and ﴿indeed, conjecture avails nothing against the truth﴾. So they named them gods and worshipped them besides God. ﴿They are only names you have named, you and your fathers, for which God has sent down no authority.﴾ ﴿Indeed, God is All-Knowing of what they do﴾, and He will recompense them for it with severe punishment.

{37} The Exalted says: {It is not possible that this Qur'an be fabricated apart from Allah}; that is, it is neither possible nor conceivable that this Qur'an be invented and attributed to Allah [Exalted is He], because it is the Great Book, "falsehood cannot approach it from before it or behind it; it is a revelation from the All-Wise, the Praiseworthy" (41:42). It is the Book that, if mankind and the jinn were to gather together to produce its like, they would not produce its like, even if they were to aid one another (17:88). It is the Book spoken by the Lord of the worlds. How then could any of creation speak its like, or anything approaching it, when speech follows the greatness of the speaker and his attributes?! If there were someone who equalled Allah in His greatness and in the attributes of His perfection, it would be possible for him to produce the like of this Qur'an. Yet even supposing, by way of hypothesis and assumption, that someone fabricated it and attributed it to the Lord of the worlds, He would hasten to punish him and swiftly seize him with retribution.

But Allah sent down this Book as a mercy to the worlds and as a proof against all the servants. He sent it down {as a confirmation of what was before it}: of the Books of Allah revealed before it, by agreeing with them and confirming them in what they testified to and what they foretold of its descent, so it came to pass as they had reported. {And a detailed explanation of the Book}: of the lawful and the unlawful, the religious and the decreed rulings, and the true reports. {There is no doubt in it, from the Lord of the worlds}; that is, there is no doubt or hesitation in it in any respect. Rather, it is the absolute truth, a revelation from the Lord of the worlds, who nurtured all creation with His blessings. Among the greatest forms of His nurturing is that He sent down to them this Book, which contains their religious and worldly interests, encompassing noble character and excellent deeds.

{38} {Or do they say}; that is, those who deny it out of obstinacy and rebellion: {"He has invented it"}: Muhammad has invented it and attributed it to Allah. {Say}: to them, binding them to something, if they are able to do it, then what they claim is possible; otherwise, their saying is false: {"Then bring a surah like it, and call upon whomever you can besides Allah, if you are truthful"}: to help you in producing a surah like it. This is impossible, and even if it were possible, they would have claimed their ability to do so and would have produced its like. But since their incapacity became evident, it became clear that what they said is false and has no share of proof.

{39} What led them to deny the Qur'an, which contains the truth above which there is no truth, is that they did not comprehend it in knowledge. Had they comprehended it in knowledge and understood it properly, they would have submitted in affirming it. Likewise, until now, its interpretation (ta'wil), which He promised would bring them the punishment and send upon them retribution, has not come to them. This denial issuing from them is of the same kind as the denial of those before them. Therefore He said: {Thus did those before them deny; so look at how was the end of the wrongdoers}: namely, the destruction that left none of them. So let these people beware of persisting in their denial, lest there befall them what befell the denying nations and the destroyed generations.
In this is evidence for deliberation in matters, and that a person should not hasten to accept or reject something before comprehending it in knowledge.

He sent it down {as a confirmation of what was before it}: of the Books of Allah revealed before it, by agreeing with them and confirming them in what they testified to and what they foretold of its descent, so it came to pass as they had reported. {And a detailed explanation of the Book}: of the lawful and the unlawful, the religious and the decreed rulings, and the true reports. {There is no doubt in it, from the Lord of the worlds}; that is, there is no doubt or hesitation in it in any respect. Rather, it is the absolute truth, a revelation from the Lord of the worlds, who nurtured all creation with His blessings. Among the greatest forms of His nurturing is that He sent down to them this Book, which contains their religious and worldly interests, encompassing noble character and excellent deeds.

{38} {Or do they say}; that is, those who deny it out of obstinacy and rebellion: {"He has invented it"}: Muhammad has invented it and attributed it to Allah. {Say}: to them, binding them to something, if they are able to do it, then what they claim is possible; otherwise, their saying is false: {"Then bring a surah like it, and call upon whomever you can besides Allah, if you are truthful"}: to help you in producing a surah like it. This is impossible, and even if it were possible, they would have claimed their ability to do so and would have produced its like. But since their incapacity became evident, it became clear that what they said is false and has no share of proof.

{39} What led them to deny the Qur'an, which contains the truth above which there is no truth, is that they did not comprehend it in knowledge. Had they comprehended it in knowledge and understood it properly, they would have submitted in affirming it. Likewise, until now, its interpretation (ta'wil), which He promised would bring them the punishment and send upon them retribution, has not come to them. This denial issuing from them is of the same kind as the denial of those before them. Therefore He said: {Thus did those before them deny; so look at how was the end of the wrongdoers}: namely, the destruction that left none of them. So let these people beware of persisting in their denial, lest there befall them what befell the denying nations and the destroyed generations.
In this is evidence for deliberation in matters, and that a person should not hasten to accept or reject something before comprehending it in knowledge.

{40} {And among them are those who believe in it}; that is, in the Qur'an and what it brought. {And among them are those who do not believe in it. And your Lord is most knowing of the corrupters}: those who do not believe in it out of wrongdoing, obstinacy, and corruption. He will requite them for their corruption with the most severe punishment.

{41} {And if they deny you}: then continue in your call, and you are not responsible for their account, nor are they responsible for yours; to each, his deed. {Say: "For me is my work, and for you is your work. You are free of what I do, and I am free of what you do"}; as the Exalted said: {Whoever does righteousness, it is for his own soul, and whoever does evil, it is against it} (41:46).

{42} He, may He be exalted, informs about some of those who denied the Messenger and what he brought: "And among them are those who listen," to the Prophet ﷺ at the time of his recitation of the revelation, not seeking guidance, but out of mere amusement, denial, and seeking out faults. This is a listening that is neither beneficial nor does it bring any good to its people. Undoubtedly, the door of success was closed to them, and they were deprived of the benefit of listening. Therefore He said: "Can you make the deaf hear, even though they do not use their reason?" This interrogative is in the sense of a firmly established negation; that is, you cannot make the deaf hear, those who do not listen to speech, even if you speak loudly to them, especially if their reason is absent. If it is impossible to make a deaf person who does not understand speech hear, then it is likewise impossible for you to make these deniers hear in a way that benefits them. As for hearing the proof, they have indeed heard that by which the conclusive proof of God is established against them. Thus this great path of knowledge, the path of what is heard concerning reports, has been closed to them.

{43} Then he mentioned the closing of the second path, which is the path of observation, saying: "And among them are those who look at you." Their looking at you does not benefit them, nor does their examining your conditions accomplish anything. Just as you cannot guide the blind, even if they do not see, so too you cannot guide these people. When their minds, hearing, and sight, which are the means that lead to knowledge and to the recognition of realities, are corrupted, then where is the path that leads them to the truth?

The words of Him, "And among them are those who look at you..." to the end of the verse, indicate that looking at the state of the Prophet ﷺ, his guidance, his character, his deeds, and what he calls to, is among the greatest proofs of his truthfulness and the soundness of what he brought, and that it suffices the one who sees clearly, without other proofs.

{44} And His saying: "Indeed, Allah does not wrong people at all," meaning He does not increase their evil deeds nor diminish their good deeds. "But people wrong themselves": the truth comes to them and they do not accept it, so Allah then punishes them by sealing their hearts, and setting a seal upon their hearing and their sight.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 10, verse 47–49:

{47} He, may He be exalted, says: ﴿And for every nation﴾ of the past nations ﴿there is a messenger﴾, who calls them to the Oneness of God and His religion. When ﴿their messenger comes to them with the clear signs﴾, some of them believe him and others deny him, and God judges between them with justice: the believers are saved and the deniers are destroyed. ﴿And they will not be wronged﴾: that they would be punished before the sending of the messenger and the establishment of the proof, or that they would be punished without their having committed a sin.

{48–49} So let those who deny you beware of resembling the nations that were destroyed, lest what befell those befall them, and let them not consider the punishment slow in coming and say: ﴿When is this promise, if you are truthful?﴾ For this is an injustice on their part, since they demand it from the Prophet (ﷺ), while he has no share in the affair at all. His duty is only to convey and to make clear to the people. As for their reckoning and the sending down of punishment upon them, that belongs to God, the Exalted. It is sent down upon them when the term He has set for it comes, and the time He has decreed for it, which accords with His divine wisdom. So when that time comes, ﴿they cannot delay it by an hour, nor can they advance it﴾. Let those who deny beware of hastening (the punishment), for they are hastening the punishment of God, which, when it descends, its force cannot be turned back from the criminal people. For this reason He said:

{50} Allah says: {Say: "Tell me, if His punishment comes upon you by night or by day, what is it that the criminals would hasten?"} That is, at the time of your sleep at night, or at a time of your heedlessness. {What is it that the criminals would hasten?} That is: what good tidings did they seek to hasten, and what punishment did they rush toward?

{51} {Is it only then, when it has befallen, that you believe in it?} Faith does not benefit at the arrival of Allah's punishment. It is said to them, as a rebuke and reproach, in that very state in which they claimed they would believe: {Is it now? Yet you were mocking it} (ta'nīb, yes, but the text reads): {Now, when you were hastening it?} For Allah's way with His servants is that He grants them the opportunity to repent when they seek it before the punishment falls; but once the punishment has fallen, faith does not benefit a soul that believes. As Allah says concerning Pharaoh when drowning overtook him: {He said, "I believe that there is no deity except the One in whom the Children of Israel believe, and I am of the Muslims."} And it is said to him: {Now? And you had disobeyed before and were among the corrupters.} And Allah says: {So their faith did not benefit them when they saw Our might. That is the way of Allah which has preceded among His servants.} And He says here: {Is it only then, when it has befallen, that you believe in it, now?} That is: you claim faith now, {and you were hastening it}. So this is what your hands have wrought, and this is what you were hastening.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 10, verses 53–56:

{53} Allah, the Exalted, says to His Prophet (ﷺ): {They ask you, "Is it true?"}; that is, the deniers ask you out of obstinacy and stubborn opposition, not out of a desire to clarify and be guided. {Is it true?}; that is, is it correct that people will be gathered and resurrected after their death for the Day of Return (ma'ad), and that servants will be recompensed for their deeds: if good, then good, and if evil, then evil? {Say}: to them, swearing to its truth and supporting it with clear evidence and proof: {Yes, by my Lord, it is indeed true}, with no doubt about it and no suspicion clinging to it, {and you cannot escape}: from Allah's power to resurrect you. Just as He began your creation when you were nothing, so He will restore you once more to recompense you for your deeds.

{54} {And} when the Resurrection comes, {if every soul that has wronged}: through disbelief and sins, possessed {all that is on the earth}: of gold, silver and other things, in order to ransom itself from the punishment of Allah, {it would surely offer it as ransom}: and it would not benefit it at all. Benefit, harm, reward and punishment depend only on righteous and evil deeds. {And they will conceal their regret}; that is, those who did wrong, {when they see the punishment}: they will regret what they had done before, but it will be too late for escape. {And it will be judged between them with justice}; that is, with complete justice, in which there is no wrong or injustice in any way.

{55} {Unquestionably, to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth}: He judges among them by His religious and decreed judgment, and He will judge among them by His judgment of recompense. For this reason He said: {Unquestionably, the promise of Allah is true, but most of them do not know}: and therefore they do not prepare for meeting Allah, and perhaps they do not even believe in it, though conclusive proofs, textual (naqli) and rational ('aqli) evidences, have come to it in abundance.

{56} {He gives life and causes death}; that is, He alone directs life and death and all other kinds of management, with no partner in that. {And to Him you will be returned}: on the Day of Resurrection, where He will recompense you for your deeds, good and evil.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 10, verses 57–58:

{57} Allah, exalted is He, says, encouraging people to turn towards this noble Book by mentioning its good qualities, which are necessary for the servants: {O mankind, there has certainly come to you an instruction from your Lord}; that is, it admonishes you and warns you against the deeds that bring about the anger of Allah and call for His punishment, and it cautions you against them by explaining their effects and corruptions. {And a healing for what is in the breasts}: this is the Qur'an, a healing for what is in the breasts, from the diseases of desires that prevent submission to the Sharia, and the diseases of doubts that undermine certain knowledge. For what it contains of admonitions, encouragement and warning, promise and threat, necessitates for the servant desire and fear. When desire for good and fear of evil are present in him and grow through the repeated arrival of the meanings of the Qur'an, this necessitates giving precedence to the will of Allah over the will of the self, and what pleases Allah becomes more beloved to the servant than the desire of his soul. Likewise, what it contains of proofs and evidences, which Allah has varied to the utmost degree of variation and explained in the finest explanation, removes the doubts that undermine the truth and brings the heart to the highest degrees of certainty. When the heart is cured of its disease and clothed in the garments of well-being, all the limbs follow it, for they are made righteous by its righteousness and corrupted by its corruption. {And guidance and mercy for the believers}: guidance is knowledge of the truth and acting upon it, and mercy is what results of good, benevolence, and reward, both immediate and deferred, for the one who is guided by it. So guidance is the most excellent means, and mercy is the most complete aim and desire. But it is not guided by it, nor is it mercy, except with respect to the believers. When guidance is attained and the mercy arising from it descends, happiness, success, profit, triumph, joy and delight are attained.

{58} For this reason Allah, exalted is He, commanded rejoicing in that, saying: {Say: "In the bounty of Allah and in His mercy"}: that is, the Qur'an, which is the greatest blessing, favour and bounty that Allah has bestowed upon His servants, and His mercy: religion, faith, the worship of Allah, love of Him and knowledge of Him. {So in that let them rejoice; it is better than what they accumulate}: than the goods and pleasures of this world. The blessing of religion, connected to the happiness of both abodes, has no comparison with everything in this world, which is perishing and passing away soon. Allah, exalted is He, commanded rejoicing in His bounty and mercy only because that necessitates the expansion and vigour of the soul, gratitude to Allah, strength, and intense desire for knowledge and faith, which calls for increasing in them both. This is praiseworthy joy, unlike joy in the desires and pleasures of this world or joy in falsehood, for that is blameworthy, as Allah said about the people of Qarun when he said to him: {Do not exult; indeed, Allah does not love the exultant}, and as Allah said about those who rejoiced in the falsehood they possessed, which contradicts what the messengers brought: {And when their messengers came to them with clear evidences, they rejoiced in what knowledge they had}.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 10, verses 57–58:

{57} Allah, exalted is He, says, encouraging people to turn towards this noble Book by mentioning its good qualities, which are necessary for the servants: {O mankind, there has certainly come to you an instruction from your Lord}; that is, it admonishes you and warns you against the deeds that bring about the anger of Allah and call for His punishment, and it cautions you against them by explaining their effects and corruptions. {And a healing for what is in the breasts}: this is the Qur'an, a healing for what is in the breasts, from the diseases of desires that prevent submission to the Sharia, and the diseases of doubts that undermine certain knowledge. Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 10, verses 59–60:

{59} Almighty God says, rebuking the polytheists who innovated the prohibition of what God has made lawful and the permission of what He has forbidden: {Say: "Have you considered what God has sent down to you of provision?"}; meaning: the kinds of animals that are lawful, which God made as provision for them and as mercy towards them. Say to them, rebuking them for this corrupt statement: {Has God permitted you, or do you fabricate against God?} It is known that God did not permit them; thus it is known that they are fabricators.

{60} {And what will be the thought of those who fabricate lies against God on the Day of Resurrection?} That is, what punishment and retribution God will inflict upon them. Almighty God says: {And on the Day of Resurrection you will see those who lied against God, their faces blackened.} {Indeed, God is full of bounty toward mankind,} abundant in grace and vast in favor. {But most of mankind are not grateful}: either they do not perform its thanks, or they use it to aid in disobeying Him, or they forbid themselves from it and reject what God has bestowed upon His servants. Few among them are the grateful, who acknowledge the blessing, praise God for it, and use it to aid in obeying Him.

From this verse, it is deduced that the basic principle regarding all foods is permissibility, except what the Revealed Law has explicitly prohibited, because God denounced those who forbade the provision He sent down to His servants.

{61} He, exalted is He, informs of His comprehensive witnessing and His awareness of all the states of His servants in their movements and their stillness, and within this is a call to be mindful of Him at all times. So He says: {And you are not engaged in any affair}; that is, any of your states, religious or worldly, {and you recite not from it any Qur'an}; that is, you do not recite from the Qur'an which Allah has revealed to you, {nor do you do any deed}, small or great, {except that We are witnesses over you when you are engaged in it}; that is, at the time you begin it and persist in acting upon it. So be mindful of Allah in your deeds, perform them sincerely and with diligence, and beware of what Allah dislikes, for He is aware of you, knowing your outward and inward states. {And not absent from your Lord is any [part] of an atom's weight within the earth or within the heaven or [anything] smaller than that or greater, but it is in a clear register}; that is, His knowledge encompasses it and His pen has run with it. These two levels are among the levels of al-qada' (divine decree) and al-qadr (divine measuring), and Allah often joins them together: the all-encompassing knowledge of all things and the all-encompassing writing of all events; as in His saying: {Do you not know that Allah knows what is in the heaven and what is in the earth? Indeed that is in a register. Indeed that, for Allah, is easy}.

Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on Surah 10, verses 62–64:

{62} He, exalted is He, informs about His allies and beloved ones, and mentions their deeds, their attributes, and their reward. He says: ﴿Verily, the allies of Allah—there is no fear for them, nor shall they grieve﴾: concerning what lies ahead of them of frightening and terrifying events, ﴿nor shall they grieve﴾ over what they have sent ahead; for they sent ahead only righteous deeds. And since there is no fear for them and they do not grieve, security, happiness, and abundant good are established for them, which none knows except Allah, exalted is He.

{63} Then He mentions their attributes, saying: ﴿those who believed﴾ in Allah, His angels, His books, His messengers, the Last Day, and the divine decree, its good and its evil, and they confirmed their faith by practicing taqwa (God-consciousness) through carrying out the commands and avoiding the prohibitions. Thus, everyone who is a believer and God-conscious is a friend (wali) of Allah, exalted is He.

{64} ﴿For them are good tidings in the worldly life and in the Hereafter﴾: As for the good tidings in this world, they are the good praise and affection in the hearts of the believers, the righteous dream, what the servant sees of Allah's kindness toward him, His facilitating for him the best deeds and character, and His turning him away from bad character. As for the Hereafter, the first of its good tidings is the glad tidings at the taking of their souls, as Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿Indeed, those who say, "Our Lord is Allah," and then remain steadfast—the angels descend upon them, [saying], "Do not fear and do not grieve, but receive good tidings of Paradise, which you were promised"﴾. In the grave, there is what they are given good news of: the pleasure of Allah, exalted is He, and lasting bliss. In the Hereafter, the good tidings are complete with entry into the Gardens of Bliss and deliverance from painful punishment. ﴿There is no alteration to the words of Allah﴾: rather, what Allah has promised is true and cannot be changed or altered, for He is the Truthful in His speech, whom no one can oppose regarding what He has decreed and decided. ﴿That is the great triumph﴾: because it includes deliverance from every harm and attaining every desired, beloved thing. He restricted triumph to it because there is no triumph for anyone other than the people of faith and taqwa.

The summary: the good tidings encompass every good and reward that Allah has ordained in this world and the Hereafter upon faith and taqwa, and for this reason He stated it absolutely without restricting it.

{65} That is: do not let the speech of the deniers grieve you, the words by which they seek to disparage you and your religion; for their words will neither grant them honour nor harm you in the least. {Indeed, honour belongs to Allah entirely}; He gives it to whomever He wills and withholds it from whomever He wills. Allah, the Exalted, says: {Whoever desires honour—then to Allah belongs all honour entirely}, that is: let him seek it through obedience to Him. The proof is His words that follow: {To Him ascend good words, and righteous deeds He raises}. It is well known that you are upon the obedience of Allah, and that honour belongs to you and to your followers from Allah. {And honour belongs to Allah, and to His Messenger, and to the believers}. As for His words {He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing}: His hearing has encompassed all voices, so nothing of them is hidden from Him; and His knowledge has encompassed all apparent and hidden things, so there is not lost from Him the weight of an atom's ounce in the heavens or on the earth, nor anything smaller than that or greater. He, the Exalted, hears your speech and the speech of your enemies about you, and knows all of that in detail. So be content with the knowledge and sufficiency of Allah; {and whoever fears Allah, He will be sufficient for him}.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 10, verse 66–67:

{66} He, may He be exalted, informs that to Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth in terms of creation, dominion and servants [and slaves], and He disposes of them as He wills through His rulings. All of them are possessions of Allah, subjected and managed, and they do not deserve any part of worship, nor are they partners of Allah in any respect whatsoever. For this reason He said: ﴿And those who call upon other than Allah do not follow partners. They follow only assumption﴾, which does not avail anything against the truth, ﴿and they are not but guessing﴾. In that there is conjecture, falsehood and slander. So if they are truthful that they are partners of Allah, let them show from their attributes that which entitles them to even an atom's weight of worship; but they will not be able to do so. Is there then anyone among them who creates anything, or provides sustenance, or possesses any of the created things, or manages the night and the day which Allah has made a means of sustenance (qiyam) for the people?!

{67} ﴿It is He who made for you the night that you may rest therein﴾: for sleep and comfort, because of the darkness that covers the face of the earth. Were the light to continue, you would neither be settled nor at rest. ﴿And﴾ Allah made ﴿the day as something to see by﴾; that is, illuminating, so that creatures may see by it and thereby carry on with their livelihoods and the affairs of their religion and their worldly life. ﴿Indeed, in that are signs for a people who hear﴾: hearing with understanding, acceptance and seeking guidance from Allah, not the hearing of obstinacy and stubbornness. Indeed, in that are signs for a people who hear, by which they derive evidence that He alone is the One worthy of worship, that He is the true God, that the divinity of anything else is false, and that He is the Most Kind, the Most Merciful, the All-Knowing, the All-Wise.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on Surah 10, verses 68–70:

{68} The Exalted says, reporting the slander of the polytheists against the Lord of the worlds: ﴿They say, "God has taken a son."﴾ He declared Himself free of this by saying ﴿Glory be to Him﴾; that is, He is exalted above what the wrongdoers say, attributing deficiencies to Him, exalted far above that. Then He proved this with several proofs. The first is His saying ﴿He is the Self-Sufficient﴾; that is, self-sufficiency is confined to Him, and all kinds of sufficiency are encompassed in Him. He is the One who has complete self-sufficiency in every respect and from every standpoint. So if He is self-sufficient in every way, why would He take a son? Is it because He needs a son? That contradicts His self-sufficiency. No one takes a son except out of a deficiency in his self-sufficiency!

The second proof is His saying ﴿To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth﴾. This is a comprehensive and general statement; nothing that exists among the inhabitants of the heavens and the earth is excluded from it. All of them are created servants and owned slaves. It is well known that this general attribute negates that He could have a son from among them, for a son is of the same kind as his father; he cannot be created or owned. So His ownership of whatever is in the heavens and the earth, in general, contradicts the idea of begetting.

The third proof is His saying ﴿You have no authority for this﴾; that is, do you have any evidence or proof that shows God has a son? If they had any proof, they would have presented it. When He challenged them and made them unable to establish a proof, it became known that what they said is false, and that it is speech without knowledge. For this reason He said ﴿Do you say about God what you do not know?﴾ Indeed, this is among the greatest of prohibited acts.

{69–70} ﴿Say: Indeed, those who invent lies against God will not succeed﴾; that is, they will not attain their aim, and their objective will not be realized. They only enjoy a little in this world in their disbelief and lying, and then they will be returned to God and go back to Him. Then He will make them taste ﴿the severe punishment because they used to disbelieve﴾. God did not wrong them, but they wronged themselves.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 10, verses 71–73:

{71} Allah the Exalted says to His Prophet: "Recite to your people the account of Noah," concerning his call to his people when he invited them to Allah for a long period. He remained among them for a thousand years less fifty years, and his calling them only increased them in transgression. So they grew weary of him and became fed up, while he, peace be upon him, was neither lax nor slack in calling them. He said to them: ﴿O my people, if my standing [among you] and my reminding you of the signs of Allah has become burdensome to you﴾; that is, if my presence among you and my reminding you of the signs of Allah, meaning the clear and manifest proofs, has become hard for you and grave in your sight, and you wish to harm me or to reject the truth, ﴿then upon Allah I have relied﴾; that is, I have depended upon Allah to repel every evil intended against me and against what I call to. This is my army and my provision. As for you, bring whatever you are able to of kinds of equipment and numbers, ﴿so determine your affair, you and your partners﴾: all of you, such that none of you stays behind and you spare none of your effort, ﴿and let not your affair be to you in confusion﴾; that is, ambiguous and hidden, but let it be manifest and open. ﴿Then carry it out against me﴾; that is, carry out against me the punishment and the harm that is within your power, ﴿and give me no respite﴾; that is, do not grant me a moment of delay from the day.

This is a decisive proof and a great sign of the soundness of his message and the truthfulness of what he brought, since he was alone, with no tribe to protect him and no soldiers to shelter him. He openly confronted his people, denouncing the foolishness of their opinions, the corruption of their religion, and the faults of their gods. They bore hatred and enmity toward him greater than the firm mountains, and they were people of power and might. He said to them: gather together, you and your partners and whomever you can, and display everything you are able of plotting, then bring it upon me if you are capable of that. Yet they were unable to do anything of the sort. Thus it is known that he was truly the truthful one, and they were the liars in what they claimed.

{72} For this reason He said: ﴿But if you turn away﴾ from what I have called you to, there is no justification for your turning away, since it has become clear that you do not turn away from falsehood to truth, but rather you turn away from truth, for which the proofs have been established, to falsehood, for which the proofs have been established as corrupt. Moreover, ﴿I have not asked you for any reward﴾ for my call or for your response, so that you might say: this man has come to take our wealth, and thus you refrain on that account. ﴿My reward is only from Allah﴾; that is, I do not seek reward or recompense except from Him. ﴿And also﴾, I have not commanded you to something and then opposed you by doing its opposite; rather, ﴿I have been commanded to be among the Muslims﴾: so I am the first to enter into it and the first to act upon what I have commanded you.

{73} ﴿But they denied him﴾ after he had called them night and day, secretly and openly, and his calling only increased them in flight. ﴿So We saved him and those with him in the ship﴾, which We commanded him to build before Our eyes, and We said to him: when the oven boils over, then load into it two of each kind, and your family, except those against whom the word has already preceded, and those who believe. He did that, and Allah commanded the sky with pouring rain, and caused the earth to gush forth with springs, so the waters met for a matter already decreed. And We carried him upon a vessel of planks and nails, running before Our eyes. ﴿And We made them successors﴾ in the earth after the destruction of the deniers, then Allah blessed his offspring and made his descendants the ones who remained, and scattered them across the regions of the earth. ﴿And We drowned those who denied Our signs﴾ after that clarification and the establishment of proof. ﴿So see how was the end of those who were warned﴾: it was destruction with disgrace and a succession of curses upon them in every generation that comes after them, so that you hear of them nothing but blame and see nothing but condemnation and reproach. Therefore let these deniers beware lest there befall them what befell those denying peoples of destruction, disgrace and punishment.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 10, verses 71–73:
