This is a decisive proof and a great sign of the soundness of his message and the truthfulness of what he brought, since he was alone, with no tribe to protect him and no soldiers to shelter him. He openly confronted his people, denouncing the foolishness of their opinions, the corruption of their religion, and the faults of their gods. They bore hatred and enmity toward him greater than the firm mountains, and they were people of power and might. He said to them: gather together, you and your partners and whomever you can, and display everything you are able of plotting, then bring it upon me if you are capable of that. Yet they were unable to do anything of the sort. Thus it is known that he was truly the truthful one, and they were the liars in what they claimed.

{72} For this reason He said: ﴿But if you turn away﴾ from what I have called you to, there is no justification for your turning away, since it has become clear that you do not turn away from falsehood to truth, but rather you turn away from truth, for which the proofs have been established, to falsehood, for which the proofs have been established as corrupt. Moreover, ﴿I have not asked you for any reward﴾ for my call or for your response, so that you might say: this man has come to take our wealth, and thus you refrain on that account. ﴿My reward is only from Allah﴾; that is, I do not seek reward or recompense except from Him. ﴿And also﴾, I have not commanded you to something and then opposed you by doing its opposite; rather, ﴿I have been commanded to be among the Muslims﴾: so I am the first to enter into it and the first to act upon what I have commanded you.

{73} ﴿But they denied him﴾ after he had called them night and day, secretly and openly, and his calling only increased them in flight. ﴿So We saved him and those with him in the ship﴾, which We commanded him to build before Our eyes, and We said to him: when the oven boils over, then load into it two of each kind, and your family, except those against whom the word has already preceded, and those who believe. He did that, and Allah commanded the sky with pouring rain, and caused the earth to gush forth with springs, so the waters met for a matter already decreed. And We carried him upon a vessel of planks and nails, running before Our eyes. ﴿And We made them successors﴾ in the earth after the destruction of the deniers, then Allah blessed his offspring and made his descendants the ones who remained, and scattered them across the regions of the earth. ﴿And We drowned those who denied Our signs﴾ after that clarification and the establishment of proof. ﴿So see how was the end of those who were warned﴾: it was destruction with disgrace and a succession of curses upon them in every generation that comes after them, so that you hear of them nothing but blame and see nothing but condemnation and reproach. Therefore let these deniers beware lest there befall them what befell those denying peoples of destruction, disgrace and punishment.

{74} That is: then after Noah (peace be upon him), We sent messengers to their peoples, those who denied, calling them to guidance and warning them against the causes of ruin. "And they came to them with clear proofs"; that is, every prophet was supported in his call with signs indicating the truth of what he brought. "But they were not going to believe in what they had denied before"; meaning: Allah, the Exalted, punished them in that when the Messenger came to them, they hastened to deny him, so Allah sealed their hearts and placed a barrier between them and faith after they had been capable of it; as Allah, the Exalted, says: "And We turn their hearts and their sight away, just as they did not believe in it the first time" [6:110]. For this reason He said here: "Thus do We seal the hearts of the transgressors"; that is, We lock them so that no good enters them. And Allah did not wrong them, but they wronged themselves by rejecting the truth when it came to them and by their earlier denial.

{75} That is: then, after these messengers whom God sent to the deniers who were destroyed, We sent **Musa** (Moses), son of Imran, the one who spoke with the All-Merciful, one of the resolute messengers (ulu al-'azm), and one of the great figures to be followed, upon whom were revealed the great and comprehensive laws. ﴿And We made his brother Harun (Aaron) a minister with him﴾. We sent them both ﴿to Pharaoh and his chiefs﴾, that is, the leading men of his state and its notables, because the common people follow their leaders. ﴿With Our signs﴾, which point to the truth of what he brought of the Oneness of God and the prohibition of worshipping other than God, the Exalted. ﴿But they behaved arrogantly towards them﴾, through injustice and haughtiness, after they had become certain of them. ﴿And they were a guilty people﴾; that is, criminality and denial were their attributes.

{76} ﴿So when the truth came to them from Us﴾: which is the greatest and most important kind of truth, and it is from God, before whose majesty necks are humbled, the Lord of the worlds who nurtures all His creation with favours. So when the truth came to them from God through the hand of Musa, they rejected it and did not accept it, and ﴿they said: "This is indeed clear sorcery."﴾ Their own ugliness, may God curse them, did not suffice them with their turning away and their rejection of it; they went further and made it the most false of falsehoods, which is sorcery whose reality is deception. Rather, they called it manifest sorcery, clear and evident, when it is the clear truth.

{77} For this reason ﴿Musa said﴾ to them, rebuking them for their rejection of the truth, which only the most unjust of people would reject: ﴿"Do you say of the truth when it has come to you: 'Is this sorcery?'"﴾ That is: do you say that it is clear sorcery? ﴿"Is this sorcery?"﴾; that is, consider its description and what it contains, for by that alone one would be certain that it is the truth. ﴿"And the sorcerers do not prosper."﴾ Neither in this world nor in the next. So look at whom the final outcome belongs to, and whom success and triumph come through. Afterwards they knew, and it became clear to everyone, that Musa, peace be upon him, was the one who prospered and won the victory of this world and the next.

{78} ﴿They said﴾ to Musa, rejecting his words with what cannot be rejected by it: ﴿"Have you come to us to turn us away from what we found our fathers following?"﴾ That is: have you come to turn us away from what we found our fathers upon, of polytheism and the worship of other than God, and to command us to worship God alone, without partner? They made the words of their misguided forefathers a proof by which they rejected the truth that Musa, peace be upon him, had brought. And His words: ﴿"And that greatness in the land should be yours?"﴾; that is: have you come to us so that you may become the leaders, and to expel us from our lands? This was deception from them, and a way of pushing their ignorant followers and inciting their common people to oppose Musa and not to believe in him. This is not an argument for one who knows the realities and distinguishes between matters, for proofs are repelled only by proofs and demonstrations. As for one who brings the truth, and whose words are rejected by such things, these show the inability of the one who raises them to bring what would refute the claim brought by his opponent; for had he had a proof, he would have presented it and would not have resorted to saying: "Your aim is such-and-such" or "your intention is such-and-such," whether he was truthful in what he said about his opponent's purpose or lying. Yet Musa, peace and blessings be upon him, everyone who knew his condition and what he called to knew that he had no aim of exalting himself in the land; his aim was like the aim of his fellow messengers, the guidance of creation and directing them to what benefits them. But the reality of the matter is as they expressed it in their words: ﴿"And we will not believe you."﴾; that is, out of arrogance and obstinacy, not because what Musa and Harun brought was false, nor because of any confusion in it, nor for any other reason besides injustice, aggression, and the desire for exaltation with which they accused Musa and Harun.

{79} ﴿And Pharaoh said﴾, opposing the truth brought by Musa and overpowering his chiefs and people: ﴿"Bring me every knowledgeable sorcerer."﴾; that is, skilled in sorcery and proficient in it. He sent throughout the cities of Egypt for whoever could bring him the various kinds of sorcerers, of different types and classes.

{80} ﴿So when the sorcerers came﴾, to contend with Musa, ﴿Musa said to them: "Throw what you are going to throw."﴾; that is, whatever you wish; I will not specify anything for you. He did this because he was certain of his victory, unconcerned with them and with what they had brought.

{81} ﴿So when they threw﴾ their ropes and staffs, which appeared as if they were snakes moving, ﴿Musa said: "What you have brought is sorcery."﴾; that is, this is real, great sorcery. Yet despite its greatness, ﴿"God will surely nullify it. God does not set right the work of corrupters."﴾ For they intended by this to support falsehood over truth, and what corruption is greater than this? So every corrupter who does a deed, schemes a plot, or employs deceit, his deed will be nullified and vanish, and even if his work has some currency for a time, its final end is perishing and annihilation. As for the reformers whose aim in their deeds is the face of God, the Exalted, and whose deeds and means are beneficial and commanded, God sets right their deeds, raises them up, and makes them grow continually.

{82} So Musa threw his staff, and it swallowed up all that they had made, so their sorcery was nullified and their falsehood vanished. ﴿And God establishes the truth by His words, though the criminals dislike it.﴾ The sorcerers were thrown down when the truth became clear to them; Pharaoh threatened them with crucifixion and the cutting off of hands and feet, but they paid no heed to that and remained steadfast in their faith.

{83} As for Pharaoh, his chiefs, and his followers, none of them believed; rather they persisted in their rebellion, wandering blindly. For this reason He said: ﴿"None believed in Musa except a few offspring of his people"﴾; that is, youths of the Children of Israel who endured fear because faith had taken root in their hearts, ﴿"out of fear of Pharaoh and their chiefs, that he would tempt them"﴾ away from their religion. ﴿"Indeed Pharaoh was haughty in the land"﴾; that is, he had domination and power in it, so it was right for them to fear his tyranny; ﴿"and indeed he was among the extravagant"﴾; that is, those who exceed the bounds in oppression and aggression. The wisdom, and God knows best, in the fact that none believed in Musa except a few offspring of his people is that offspring and youths are more receptive to the truth and quicker to submit to it, unlike the elders and others who were raised in disbelief, for because of the corrupt beliefs that remained in their hearts, they are further from the truth than others.

{84} ﴿And Musa said﴾, enjoining his people to patience and reminding them of what would help them endure it: ﴿"O my people, if you have believed in God, then rely upon Him, if you are Muslims."﴾ That is: fulfil the duty of faith, rely upon Him, turn to Him, and seek His help.

{85} ﴿They said, complying with that: "In God we have put our trust. Our Lord, do not make us a trial for the wrongdoing people."﴾ That is: do not give them power over us so that they tempt us or overcome us, and so they are tempted by that and say: "If they were upon the truth, they would not have been overcome."

{86} ﴿"And deliver us by Your mercy from the disbelieving people."﴾ So that we may be safe from their evil, and so that we may establish our religion in a manner by which we can establish its laws and manifest them without opposition or rivalry.

{87} ﴿And We revealed to Musa and his brother﴾, when the matter grew severe for their people from Pharaoh and his people, who were eager to tempt them away from their religion, ﴿"that you two settle your people in Egypt in houses"﴾; that is, command them to make for themselves houses in which they can conceal themselves. ﴿"And make your houses into places of prayer"﴾; that is, make them places where you pray when you are unable to establish prayer in churches and public houses of worship. ﴿"And establish prayer"﴾, for it is an aid in all matters. ﴿"And give good tidings to the believers"﴾ of victory, support, and the manifestation of their religion, for ﴿with hardship comes ease; indeed, with hardship comes ease.﴾ When the distress intensified and the matter became narrow, God relieved it and widened it.

{88} When Musa saw the hardness and turning away from Pharaoh and his chiefs, he invoked against them, and Harun said "Amen" to his supplication. He said: ﴿"Our Lord, You have given Pharaoh and his chiefs adornment"﴾, with which they adorned themselves: various kinds of jewelry, garments, decorated houses, splendid mounts, and servants, ﴿"and wealth"﴾: great ﴿"in the life of this world. Our Lord, so that they lead [people] astray from Your way."﴾ That is: they used their wealth only to lead astray from Your way, so they went astray and led others astray. ﴿"Our Lord, obliterate their wealth"﴾; that is, destroy it for them, either by ruin or by turning it into stones from which no benefit can be gained. ﴿"And harden their hearts"﴾; that is, make them hard. ﴿"So that they do not believe until they see the painful punishment."﴾ He said this in anger at them, because they had dared to violate the sanctities of God, corrupted the servants of God, and barred [people] from His way. And, out of his complete knowledge of his Lord, that God would punish them for what they had done by closing the door of faith upon them.

{89} ﴿God, the Exalted, said: "Your supplication has been answered."﴾ This is evidence that Musa supplicated and Harun said "Amen" to his supplication, and that the one who says "Amen" is a partner of the supplicant in that supplication. ﴿"So be steadfast"﴾ in your religion, and continue in your call, ﴿"and do not follow the way of those who do not know"﴾; that is, do not follow the path of the ignorant and misguided, who deviate from the straight path and follow the ways of Hellfire.

{90} God commanded Musa to journey by night with the Children of Israel, and informed him that they would follow him. Pharaoh sent into the cities summoners saying: "Indeed these are a small band"; that is, Musa and his people, "and indeed they have enraged us, and indeed we are a vigilant host." So he gathered his armies, the far and the near, and he pursued them with his troops, out of rebellion and enmity; that is, going out to them as aggressors against Musa and his people, and transgressing in the land. When rebellion grows strong and sin is entrenched, await punishment. ﴿And We brought the Children of Israel across the sea﴾. This was because God revealed to Musa, when he reached the sea, that he should strike it with his staff; he struck it, and it split into twelve paths, and the Children of Israel traversed it, while Pharaoh and his troops pursued them, entering behind them. When Musa and his people had completed their exit from the sea, and Pharaoh and his troops had entered it, God commanded the sea, and it closed over Pharaoh and his troops, drowning them while the Children of Israel looked on. When drowning overtook Pharaoh and he was certain of his destruction, ﴿he said: "I believe that there is no deity except the One in whom the Children of Israel believe"﴾, who is God, the true deity, besides whom there is no deity, ﴿"and I am among the Muslims"﴾; that is, those who submit to the religion of God and to what Musa brought.

{91} God, the Exalted, said, clarifying that this faith in this state is of no benefit to him: ﴿"Now? And you had disobeyed before, and you were among the corrupters."﴾; that is, you openly defied with sins, disbelief, and denial, ﴿so faith will not benefit you﴾. This is God's custom: when disbelievers reach this compelled state, their faith does not benefit them, because their faith becomes faith by sight, like the faith of one who arrives at the Resurrection, whereas what benefits is faith in the unseen.

{92} ﴿"Today We shall deliver your body, that you may be a sign for those after you."﴾ The commentators said: because of the great terror of Pharaoh in their hearts, the Children of Israel seemed not to believe his drowning, and doubted it. So God commanded the sea to cast him up on a high shore with his body, to be for them a lesson and a sign. ﴿"And indeed, many of the people are heedless of Our signs."﴾ Therefore these signs pass over them and are repeated, yet they do not benefit from them, because they do not turn towards them. As for one who has intellect and an attentive heart, he sees in the signs of God what is the greatest proof of the truth of what the messengers reported.

{93} ﴿And We settled the Children of Israel in a good settlement﴾; that is, God lodged them and housed them in the dwellings of Pharaoh's family, and made them heirs to their land and homes. ﴿And We provided them with good things﴾: foods, drinks, and other things. ﴿Yet they did not differ﴾ concerning the truth ﴿until knowledge came to them﴾, which should have brought about their unity and harmony. This is the disease that afflicts the people of sound religion: when Satan cannot make them abandon religion entirely, he strives to sow discord among them and to cast enmity and hatred, so that the differences which lead to this arise, and then misguidance of some by others and enmity among them occur, which is the delight of the accursed one. Otherwise, if their Lord is one, their Messenger is one, their religion is one, and their common interests are united, then why would they differ in a way that scatters their unity, disperses their affairs, and dissolves their bond and order, thereby losing from their religious and worldly interests what is lost, and so losing from their religion what is lost because of it? We ask You, O God, for gentleness toward Your believing servants, that You gather their unity, mend their rift, and bring back their distant ones to their near ones, O Possessor of Majesty and Honour!

{85} ﴿They said, complying with that: "In God we have put our trust. {86} ﴿"And deliver us by Your mercy from the disbelieving people."﴾ So that we may be safe from their evil, and so that we may establish our religion in a manner by which we can establish its laws and manifest them without opposition or rivalry.

{87} ﴿And We revealed to Musa and his brother﴾, when the matter grew severe for their people from Pharaoh and his people, who were eager to tempt them away from their religion, ﴿"that you two settle your people in Egypt in houses"﴾; that is, command them to make for themselves houses in which they can conceal themselves. ﴿"And make your houses into places of prayer"﴾; that is, make them places where you pray when you are unable to establish prayer in churches and public houses of worship. ﴿"And establish prayer"﴾, for it is an aid in all matters. ﴿"And give good tidings to the believers"﴾ of victory, support, and the manifestation of their religion, for ﴿with hardship comes ease; indeed, with hardship comes ease.﴾ When the distress intensified and the matter became narrow, God relieved it and widened it.

{90} God commanded Musa to journey by night with the Children of Israel, and informed him that they would follow him. {90} God commanded Musa to journey by night with the Children of Israel, and informed him that they would follow him. Pharaoh sent into the cities summoners saying: "Indeed these are a small band"; that is, Musa and his people, "and indeed they have enraged us, and indeed we are a vigilant host." So he gathered his armies, the far and the near, and he pursued them with his troops, out of rebellion and enmity; that is, going out to them as aggressors against Musa and his people, and transgressing in the land. This was because God revealed to Musa, when he reached the sea, that he should strike it with his staff; he struck it, and it split into twelve paths, and the Children of Israel traversed it, while Pharaoh and his troops pursued them, entering behind them. When Musa and his people had completed their exit from the sea, and Pharaoh and his troops had entered it, God commanded the sea, and it closed over Pharaoh and his troops, drowning them while the Children of Israel looked on. When drowning overtook Pharaoh and he was certain of his destruction, ﴿he said: "I believe that there is no deity except the One in whom the Children of Israel believe"﴾, who is God, the true deity, besides whom there is no deity, ﴿"and I am among the Muslims"﴾; that is, those who submit to the religion of God and to what Musa brought.

{91} God, the Exalted, said, clarifying that this faith in this state is of no benefit to him: ﴿"Now? And you had disobeyed before, and you were among the corrupters."﴾; that is, you openly defied with sins, disbelief, and denial, ﴿so faith will not benefit you﴾. {92} ﴿"Today We shall deliver your body, that you may be a sign for those after you."﴾ The commentators said: because of the great terror of Pharaoh in their hearts, the Children of Israel seemed not to believe his drowning, and doubted it. As for one who has intellect and an attentive heart, he sees in the signs of God what is the greatest proof of the truth of what the messengers reported.

{93} ﴿And We settled the Children of Israel in a good settlement﴾; that is, God lodged them and housed them in the dwellings of Pharaoh's family, and made them heirs to their land and homes. ﴿And We provided them with good things﴾: foods, drinks, and other things. ﴿Yet they did not differ﴾ concerning the truth ﴿until knowledge came to them﴾, which should have brought about their unity and harmony. But some of them transgressed against others, and many of them developed desires and aims that contradicted the truth, so much difference arose among them. ﴿Indeed your Lord will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection concerning that wherein they used to differ﴾, by His just judgment that arises from His complete knowledge and all-encompassing power.

This is the disease that afflicts the people of sound religion: when Satan cannot make them abandon religion entirely, he strives to sow discord among them and to cast enmity and hatred, so that the differences which lead to this arise, and then misguidance of some by others and enmity among them occur, which is the delight of the accursed one. We ask You, O God, for gentleness toward Your believing servants, that You gather their unity, mend their rift, and bring back their distant ones to their near ones, O Possessor of Majesty and Honour!

{75} That is: then, after these messengers whom God sent to the deniers who were destroyed, We sent **Musa** (Moses), son of Imran, the one who spoke with the All-Merciful, one of the resolute messengers (ulu al-'azm), and one of the great figures to be followed, upon whom were revealed the great and comprehensive laws. ﴿And We made his brother Harun (Aaron) a minister with him﴾. {76} ﴿So when the truth came to them from Us﴾: which is the greatest and most important kind of truth, and it is from God, before whose majesty necks are humbled, the Lord of the worlds who nurtures all His creation with favours. Pharaoh sent into the cities summoners saying: "Indeed these are a small band"; that is, Musa and his people, "and indeed they have enraged us, and indeed we are a vigilant host." So he gathered his armies, the far and the near, and he pursued them with his troops, out of rebellion and enmity; that is, going out to them as aggressors against Musa and his people, and transgressing in the land. This was because God revealed to Musa, when he reached the sea, that he should strike it with his staff; he struck it, and it split into twelve paths, and the Children of Israel traversed it, while Pharaoh and his troops pursued them, entering behind them. When Musa and his people had completed their exit from the sea, and Pharaoh and his troops had entered it, God commanded the sea, and it closed over Pharaoh and his troops, drowning them while the Children of Israel looked on. When drowning overtook Pharaoh and he was certain of his destruction, ﴿he said: "I believe that there is no deity except the One in whom the Children of Israel believe"﴾, who is God, the true deity, besides whom there is no deity, ﴿"and I am among the Muslims"﴾; that is, those who submit to the religion of God and to what Musa brought.

{91} God, the Exalted, said, clarifying that this faith in this state is of no benefit to him: ﴿"Now? And you had disobeyed before, and you were among the corrupters."﴾; that is, you openly defied with sins, disbelief, and denial, ﴿so faith will not benefit you﴾. This is God's custom: when disbelievers reach this compelled state, their faith does not benefit them, because their faith becomes faith by sight, like the faith of one who arrives at the Resurrection, whereas what benefits is faith in the unseen.

{92} ﴿"Today We shall deliver your body, that you may be a sign for those after you."﴾ The commentators said: because of the great terror of Pharaoh in their hearts, the Children of Israel seemed not to believe his drowning, and doubted it. So God commanded the sea to cast him up on a high shore with his body, to be for them a lesson and a sign. ﴿"And indeed, many of the people are heedless of Our signs."﴾ Therefore these signs pass over them and are repeated, yet they do not benefit from them, because they do not turn towards them. As for one who has intellect and an attentive heart, he sees in the signs of God what is the greatest proof of the truth of what the messengers reported.

{93} ﴿And We settled the Children of Israel in a good settlement﴾; that is, God lodged them and housed them in the dwellings of Pharaoh's family, and made them heirs to their land and homes. ﴿And We provided them with good things﴾: foods, drinks, and other things. ﴿Yet they did not differ﴾ concerning the truth ﴿until knowledge came to them﴾, which should have brought about their unity and harmony. But some of them transgressed against others, and many of them developed desires and aims that contradicted the truth, so much difference arose among them. ﴿Indeed your Lord will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection concerning that wherein they used to differ﴾, by His just judgment that arises from His complete knowledge and all-encompassing power.

This is the disease that afflicts the people of sound religion: when Satan cannot make them abandon religion entirely, he strives to sow discord among them and to cast enmity and hatred, so that the differences which lead to this arise, and then misguidance of some by others and enmity among them occur, which is the delight of the accursed one. We ask You, O God, for gentleness toward Your believing servants, that You gather their unity, mend their rift, and bring back their distant ones to their near ones, O Possessor of Majesty and Honour!

{75} That is: then, after these messengers whom God sent to the deniers who were destroyed, We sent **Musa** (Moses), son of Imran, the one who spoke with the All-Merciful, one of the resolute messengers (ulu al-'azm), and one of the great figures to be followed, upon whom were revealed the great and comprehensive laws. ﴿And We made his brother Harun (Aaron) a minister with him﴾. {76} ﴿So when the truth came to them from Us﴾: which is the greatest and most important kind of truth, and it is from God, before whose majesty necks are humbled, the Lord of the worlds who nurtures all His creation with favours. {79} ﴿And Pharaoh said﴾, opposing the truth brought by Musa and overpowering his chiefs and people: ﴿"Bring me every knowledgeable sorcerer."﴾; that is, skilled in sorcery and proficient in it. {80} ﴿So when the sorcerers came﴾, to contend with Musa, ﴿Musa said to them: "Throw what you are going to throw."﴾; that is, whatever you wish; I will not specify anything for you. He did this because he was certain of his victory, unconcerned with them and with what they had brought.

{75} That is: then, after these messengers whom God sent to the deniers who were destroyed, We sent **Musa** (Moses), son of Imran, the one who spoke with the All-Merciful, one of the resolute messengers (ulu al-'azm), and one of the great figures to be followed, upon whom were revealed the great and comprehensive laws. ﴿And We made his brother Harun (Aaron) a minister with him﴾. We sent them both ﴿to Pharaoh and his chiefs﴾, that is, the leading men of his state and its notables, because the common people follow their leaders. ﴿With Our signs﴾, which point to the truth of what he brought of the Oneness of God and the prohibition of worshipping other than God, the Exalted. ﴿But they behaved arrogantly towards them﴾, through injustice and haughtiness, after they had become certain of them. ﴿And they were a guilty people﴾; that is, criminality and denial were their attributes.

{76} ﴿So when the truth came to them from Us﴾: which is the greatest and most important kind of truth, and it is from God, before whose majesty necks are humbled, the Lord of the worlds who nurtures all His creation with favours. So when the truth came to them from God through the hand of Musa, they rejected it and did not accept it, and ﴿they said: "This is indeed clear sorcery."﴾ Their own ugliness, may God curse them, did not suffice them with their turning away and their rejection of it; they went further and made it the most false of falsehoods, which is sorcery whose reality is deception. Rather, they called it manifest sorcery, clear and evident, when it is the clear truth.

{77} For this reason ﴿Musa said﴾ to them, rebuking them for their rejection of the truth, which only the most unjust of people would reject: ﴿"Do you say of the truth when it has come to you: 'Is this sorcery?'"﴾ That is: do you say that it is clear sorcery? ﴿"Is this sorcery?"﴾; that is, consider its description and what it contains, for by that alone one would be certain that it is the truth. ﴿"And the sorcerers do not prosper."﴾ Neither in this world nor in the next. So look at whom the final outcome belongs to, and whom success and triumph come through. Afterwards they knew, and it became clear to everyone, that Musa, peace be upon him, was the one who prospered and won the victory of this world and the next.

{78} ﴿They said﴾ to Musa, rejecting his words with what cannot be rejected by it: ﴿"Have you come to us to turn us away from what we found our fathers following?"﴾ That is: have you come to turn us away from what we found our fathers upon, of polytheism and the worship of other than God, and to command us to worship God alone, without partner? They made the words of their misguided forefathers a proof by which they rejected the truth that Musa, peace be upon him, had brought. And His words: ﴿"And that greatness in the land should be yours?"﴾; that is: have you come to us so that you may become the leaders, and to expel us from our lands? This was deception from them, and a way of pushing their ignorant followers and inciting their common people to oppose Musa and not to believe in him. This is not an argument for one who knows the realities and distinguishes between matters, for proofs are repelled only by proofs and demonstrations. As for one who brings the truth, and whose words are rejected by such things, these show the inability of the one who raises them to bring what would refute the claim brought by his opponent; for had he had a proof, he would have presented it and would not have resorted to saying: "Your aim is such-and-such" or "your intention is such-and-such," whether he was truthful in what he said about his opponent's purpose or lying. Yet Musa, peace and blessings be upon him, everyone who knew his condition and what he called to knew that he had no aim of exalting himself in the land; his aim was like the aim of his fellow messengers, the guidance of creation and directing them to what benefits them. But the reality of the matter is as they expressed it in their words: ﴿"And we will not believe you."﴾; that is, out of arrogance and obstinacy, not because what Musa and Harun brought was false, nor because of any confusion in it, nor for any other reason besides injustice, aggression, and the desire for exaltation with which they accused Musa and Harun.

{79} ﴿And Pharaoh said﴾, opposing the truth brought by Musa and overpowering his chiefs and people: ﴿"Bring me every knowledgeable sorcerer."﴾; that is, skilled in sorcery and proficient in it. He sent throughout the cities of Egypt for whoever could bring him the various kinds of sorcerers, of different types and classes.

{80} ﴿So when the sorcerers came﴾, to contend with Musa, ﴿Musa said to them: "Throw what you are going to throw."﴾; that is, whatever you wish; I will not specify anything for you. He did this because he was certain of his victory, unconcerned with them and with what they had brought.

{81} ﴿So when they threw﴾ their ropes and staffs, which appeared as if they were snakes moving, ﴿Musa said: "What you have brought is sorcery."﴾; that is, this is real, great sorcery. Yet despite its greatness, ﴿"God will surely nullify it. God does not set right the work of corrupters."﴾ For they intended by this to support falsehood over truth, and what corruption is greater than this? So every corrupter who does a deed, schemes a plot, or employs deceit, his deed will be nullified and vanish, and even if his work has some currency for a time, its final end is perishing and annihilation. As for the reformers whose aim in their deeds is the face of God, the Exalted, and whose deeds and means are beneficial and commanded, God sets right their deeds, raises them up, and makes them grow continually.

{82} So Musa threw his staff, and it swallowed up all that they had made, so their sorcery was nullified and their falsehood vanished. ﴿And God establishes the truth by His words, though the criminals dislike it.﴾ The sorcerers were thrown down when the truth became clear to them; Pharaoh threatened them with crucifixion and the cutting off of hands and feet, but they paid no heed to that and remained steadfast in their faith.

{83} As for Pharaoh, his chiefs, and his followers, none of them believed; rather they persisted in their rebellion, wandering blindly. For this reason He said: ﴿"None believed in Musa except a few offspring of his people"﴾; that is, youths of the Children of Israel who endured fear because faith had taken root in their hearts, ﴿"out of fear of Pharaoh and their chiefs, that he would tempt them"﴾ away from their religion. ﴿"Indeed Pharaoh was haughty in the land"﴾; that is, he had domination and power in it, so it was right for them to fear his tyranny; ﴿"and indeed he was among the extravagant"﴾; that is, those who exceed the bounds in oppression and aggression. The wisdom, and God knows best, in the fact that none believed in Musa except a few offspring of his people is that offspring and youths are more receptive to the truth and quicker to submit to it, unlike the elders and others who were raised in disbelief, for because of the corrupt beliefs that remained in their hearts, they are further from the truth than others.

{84} ﴿And Musa said﴾, enjoining his people to patience and reminding them of what would help them endure it: ﴿"O my people, if you have believed in God, then rely upon Him, if you are Muslims."﴾ That is: fulfil the duty of faith, rely upon Him, turn to Him, and seek His help.

{85} ﴿They said, complying with that: "In God we have put our trust. Our Lord, do not make us a trial for the wrongdoing people."﴾ That is: do not give them power over us so that they tempt us or overcome us, and so they are tempted by that and say: "If they were upon the truth, they would not have been overcome."

{86} ﴿"And deliver us by Your mercy from the disbelieving people."﴾ So that we may be safe from their evil, and so that we may establish our religion in a manner by which we can establish its laws and manifest them without opposition or rivalry.

{87} ﴿And We revealed to Musa and his brother﴾, when the matter grew severe for their people from Pharaoh and his people, who were eager to tempt them away from their religion, ﴿"that you two settle your people in Egypt in houses"﴾; that is, command them to make for themselves houses in which they can conceal themselves. ﴿"And make your houses into places of prayer"﴾; that is, make them places where you pray when you are unable to establish prayer in churches and public houses of worship. ﴿"And establish prayer"﴾, for it is an aid in all matters. ﴿"And give good tidings to the believers"﴾ of victory, support, and the manifestation of their religion, for ﴿with hardship comes ease; indeed, with hardship comes ease.﴾ When the distress intensified and the matter became narrow, God relieved it and widened it.

{88} When Musa saw the hardness and turning away from Pharaoh and his chiefs, he invoked against them, and Harun said "Amen" to his supplication. He said: ﴿"Our Lord, You have given Pharaoh and his chiefs adornment"﴾, with which they adorned themselves: various kinds of jewelry, garments, decorated houses, splendid mounts, and servants, ﴿"and wealth"﴾: great ﴿"in the life of this world. Our Lord, so that they lead [people] astray from Your way."﴾ That is: they used their wealth only to lead astray from Your way, so they went astray and led others astray. ﴿"Our Lord, obliterate their wealth"﴾; that is, destroy it for them, either by ruin or by turning it into stones from which no benefit can be gained. ﴿"And harden their hearts"﴾; that is, make them hard. ﴿"So that they do not believe until they see the painful punishment."﴾ He said this in anger at them, because they had dared to violate the sanctities of God, corrupted the servants of God, and barred [people] from His way. And, out of his complete knowledge of his Lord, that God would punish them for what they had done by closing the door of faith upon them.

{89} ﴿God, the Exalted, said: "Your supplication has been answered."﴾ This is evidence that Musa supplicated and Harun said "Amen" to his supplication, and that the one who says "Amen" is a partner of the supplicant in that supplication. ﴿"So be steadfast"﴾ in your religion, and continue in your call, ﴿"and do not follow the way of those who do not know"﴾; that is, do not follow the path of the ignorant and misguided, who deviate from the straight path and follow the ways of Hellfire.

{90} God commanded Musa to journey by night with the Children of Israel, and informed him that they would follow him. Pharaoh sent into the cities summoners saying: "Indeed these are a small band"; that is, Musa and his people, "and indeed they have enraged us, and indeed we are a vigilant host." So he gathered his armies, the far and the near, and he pursued them with his troops, out of rebellion and enmity; that is, going out to them as aggressors against Musa and his people, and transgressing in the land. When rebellion grows strong and sin is entrenched, await punishment. ﴿And We brought the Children of Israel across the sea﴾. This was because God revealed to Musa, when he reached the sea, that he should strike it with his staff; he struck it, and it split into twelve paths, and the Children of Israel traversed it, while Pharaoh and his troops pursued them, entering behind them. When Musa and his people had completed their exit from the sea, and Pharaoh and his troops had entered it, God commanded the sea, and it closed over Pharaoh and his troops, drowning them while the Children of Israel looked on. When drowning overtook Pharaoh and he was certain of his destruction, ﴿he said: "I believe that there is no deity except the One in whom the Children of Israel believe"﴾, who is God, the true deity, besides whom there is no deity, ﴿"and I am among the Muslims"﴾; that is, those who submit to the religion of God and to what Musa brought.

{91} God, the Exalted, said, clarifying that this faith in this state is of no benefit to him: ﴿"Now? And you had disobeyed before, and you were among the corrupters."﴾; that is, you openly defied with sins, disbelief, and denial, ﴿so faith will not benefit you﴾. This is God's custom: when disbelievers reach this compelled state, their faith does not benefit them, because their faith becomes faith by sight, like the faith of one who arrives at the Resurrection, whereas what benefits is faith in the unseen.

{92} ﴿"Today We shall deliver your body, that you may be a sign for those after you."﴾ The commentators said: because of the great terror of Pharaoh in their hearts, the Children of Israel seemed not to believe his drowning, and doubted it. So God commanded the sea to cast him up on a high shore with his body, to be for them a lesson and a sign. ﴿"And indeed, many of the people are heedless of Our signs."﴾ Therefore these signs pass over them and are repeated, yet they do not benefit from them, because they do not turn towards them. As for one who has intellect and an attentive heart, he sees in the signs of God what is the greatest proof of the truth of what the messengers reported.

{93} ﴿And We settled the Children of Israel in a good settlement﴾; that is, God lodged them and housed them in the dwellings of Pharaoh's family, and made them heirs to their land and homes. ﴿And We provided them with good things﴾: foods, drinks, and other things. ﴿Yet they did not differ﴾ concerning the truth ﴿until knowledge came to them﴾, which should have brought about their unity and harmony. But some of them transgressed against others, and many of them developed desires and aims that contradicted the truth, so much difference arose among them. ﴿Indeed your Lord will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection concerning that wherein they used to differ﴾, by His just judgment that arises from His complete knowledge and all-encompassing power.

This is the disease that afflicts the people of sound religion: when Satan cannot make them abandon religion entirely, he strives to sow discord among them and to cast enmity and hatred, so that the differences which lead to this arise, and then misguidance of some by others and enmity among them occur, which is the delight of the accursed one. Otherwise, if their Lord is one, their Messenger is one, their religion is one, and their common interests are united, then why would they differ in a way that scatters their unity, disperses their affairs, and dissolves their bond and order, thereby losing from their religious and worldly interests what is lost, and so losing from their religion what is lost because of it? We ask You, O God, for gentleness toward Your believing servants, that You gather their unity, mend their rift, and bring back their distant ones to their near ones, O Possessor of Majesty and Honour!

{94} Almighty God says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): {If you are in doubt about what We have sent down to you}, whether it is true or not, {then ask those who have been reading the Scripture before you}. That is, ask the fair-minded People of the Book and the firmly grounded scholars, for they will affirm to you the truth of what you have reported and its agreement with what they possess.

It may be said: many of the People of the Book, Jews and Christians, indeed perhaps most of them, or the majority of them, denied the Messenger of God, opposed him, and rejected his call. Yet God commanded His Messenger to seek their testimony and made their testimony a proof for what he brought and an evidence of his truthfulness. How, then, can this be? The answer to this has several aspects:

Among them: when testimony is attributed to a group, or to the adherents of a creed, a land, or the like, it refers only to their upright and truthful members. As for others, even if they are more numerous, they are not taken into account, because testimony is based on integrity and truthfulness. This was realized through the faith of many of their rabbis, such as Abdullah ibn Salam and his companions, and many who embraced Islam in the time of the Prophet (ﷺ), his successors, and those after them.

Among them: the testimony of the People of the Book to the Messenger is based on their Scripture, the Torah, to which they trace their lineage. If the Torah contains what agrees with the Qur'an, confirms it, and bears witness to its truth, then even if they all, from first to last, agreed to deny that, it would not undermine what the Messenger brought.

Among them: God commanded His Messenger to call upon the People of the Book to witness to the soundness of what came to him, and this was made public and proclaimed before the assembled multitudes. It is known that many of them are among the people most eager to nullify the call of the Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ). Had they possessed anything to refute what God mentioned, they would have revealed, displayed, and clarified it. Since nothing of that happened, the failure of the opponent to refute and the acquiescence of the one who responds is among the strongest proofs of the soundness and truthfulness of this Qur'an.

Among them: most of the People of the Book did not reject the Messenger's call; rather, most of them responded to it and submitted willingly and by choice. The Messenger was sent when most of the religious people of the earth were People of the Book, and within a not very long period his religion spread, so that most of the people of Syria, Egypt, Iraq, and the lands adjoining them, which were the seats of the People of the Book's religion, submitted to Islam. None remained except the leaders who preferred their positions over the truth, and the ignorant common folk who followed them, and those who adhered nominally, without substance, to their religion, such as the Franks, whose true condition is that they are materialists who have departed from all the religions of the messengers; they have only attached themselves to Christianity in order to promote their kingdom and disguise their falsehood, as is known to whoever knows their clear and manifest conditions.

As for His saying {The truth has certainly come to you}, that is, that which is free of doubt in every respect, {from your Lord, so do not be among the doubters}: like His saying: {A Book has been sent down to you, so let there be no discomfort in your breast concerning it}.

{95} {And do not be among those who deny the signs of God, [for] you would be among the losers}. The summary of this is that God forbade two things: doubt concerning this Qur'an, and disputing about it. More severe than that is denial of it, that is, of the clear signs of God, which admit of denial in no respect. He made this result in loss, which is the absence of any gain at all, through the forfeiting of reward in this world and the Hereafter and the incurring of punishment in this world and the Hereafter. The prohibition of a thing is a command to its opposite, so it amounts to a command to full belief in the Qur'an, the heart's tranquility in it, and devotion to it in knowledge and action. Through that, the servant becomes among the gainers, who attain the most exalted aims, the best desires, and the most complete virtues, and from whom loss is removed.

{95} {And do not be among those who deny the signs of God, [for] you would be among the losers}. Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 10, verses 96–97:

{96–97} He, exalted is He, says: ﴿Indeed, those upon whom the word of your Lord has been fulfilled﴾; that is, they are among the astray and the deviant, the people of the Fire, who must come to what Allah has decreed and ordained. So they will not believe even if every sign should come to them, and the signs increase them only in transgression and deviation upon their deviation. Allah did not wrong them, but they wronged themselves by rejecting the truth when it first came to them. So Allah punished them by setting a seal upon their hearts, their hearing, and their sight, so that they do not believe until they see the painful punishment they were promised. At that time they will know with certainty that what they were upon was misguidance, and that what the messengers brought was the truth, but at a time when their faith will avail them nothing. So on that Day, ﴿the excuse of those who wronged will not benefit them, nor will they be allowed to make amends﴾. As for the signs, they benefit ﴿whoever has a heart, or gives ear while he is a witness﴾.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 10, verses 96–97:

{96–97} He, exalted is He, says: ﴿Indeed, those upon whom the word of your Lord has been fulfilled﴾; that is, they are among the astray and the deviant, the people of the Fire, who must come to what Allah has decreed and ordained. So they will not believe even if every sign should come to them, and the signs increase them only in transgression and deviation upon their deviation. Allah did not wrong them, but they wronged themselves by rejecting the truth when it first came to them. So Allah punished them by setting a seal upon their hearts, their hearing, and their sight, so that they do not believe until they see the painful punishment they were promised. At that time they will know with certainty that what they were upon was misguidance, and that what the messengers brought was the truth, but at a time when their faith will avail them nothing. So on that Day, ﴿the excuse of those who wronged will not benefit them, nor will they be allowed to make amends﴾. As for the signs, they benefit ﴿whoever has a heart, or gives ear while he is a witness﴾.

{98} The Exalted says: "Why was there not a town (qaryah) among the towns of the deniers" [who believed] "when they saw the punishment, so that its faith benefited it?" That is, none of them benefited from their faith when they saw the punishment, as the Exalted said about Pharaoh, mentioned earlier, when he said: "I believe that there is no god except the One in whom the Children of Israel believe, and I am among the Muslims." It was said to him: "Now? And you had disobeyed before and were among the corrupters." [Qur'an 10:90–91] And as the Exalted said: "So when Our punishment came to them, they said, 'We believe in Allah alone and disbelieve in what we used to associate with Him.' But their faith did not benefit them when they saw Our punishment. [This is] the way of Allah which has preceded among His servants." [Qur'an 40:84–85] And the Exalted said: "[Until], when death comes to one of them, he says, 'My Lord, send me back, that I might do righteousness in what I have left behind.' No! It is merely a word he is saying." [Qur'an 23:99–100] The wisdom in this is evident, for compelled faith is not true faith, and even if the punishment and the matter that compelled him to faith were removed from him, he would return to disbelief.

As for His saying: "Except the people of Yunus; when they believed after they had seen the punishment, We removed from them the punishment of disgrace in the worldly life and gave them enjoyment for a time" [Qur'an 10:98]: they are excepted from the preceding generality, and there must be a wisdom for that known to the One who knows the unseen and the witnessed, which has not reached us and which our understandings have not grasped. The Exalted said: "And indeed, Yunus was among the messengers... " up to His saying: "And We sent him to one hundred thousand or more. And they believed, so We gave them enjoyment for a time." [Qur'an 37:139–148]

Perhaps the wisdom in that is that if others among the destroyed had been returned, they would have gone back to what they were forbidden. As for the people of Yunus, Allah knew that their faith would continue, and indeed it did continue in fact, and they remained steadfast upon it. And Allah knows best.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 10, verses 99–100:

{99} The Exalted says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): ﴿And if your Lord had willed, those on earth would have believed, all of them entirely.﴾ That is, He would have inspired them with faith and inclined their hearts toward piety. His power is capable of that, but His wisdom required that some of them be believers and some of them disbelievers. ﴿Then, would you compel the people until they become believers?﴾ That is, you cannot do that, it is not within your capacity, and no one other than Allah has any power over any of that.

{100} ﴿And it is not for a soul to believe except by the permission of Allah﴾: by His will, His purpose, and His permission, both the decreed (qadari) and the legislated (shar'i). Whoever among the creatures is receptive to that, faith grows within him; Allah grants him success and guides him. ﴿And He places defilement﴾: that is, evil and misguidance ﴿upon those who do not reason﴾ about Allah's commands and prohibitions, and who pay no heed to His advice and admonitions.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 10, verses 99–100:

{99} The Exalted says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): ﴿And if your Lord had willed, those on earth would have believed, all of them entirely.﴾ That is, He would have inspired them with faith and inclined their hearts toward piety. His power is capable of that, but His wisdom required that some of them be believers and some of them disbelievers. ﴿Then, would you compel the people until they become believers?﴾ That is, you cannot do that, it is not within your capacity, and no one other than Allah has any power over any of that.

{100} ﴿And it is not for a soul to believe except by the permission of Allah﴾: by His will, His purpose, and His permission, both the decreed (qadari) and the legislated (shar'i). Whoever among the creatures is receptive to that, faith grows within him; Allah grants him success and guides him. ﴿And He places defilement﴾: that is, evil and misguidance ﴿upon those who do not reason﴾ about Allah's commands and prohibitions, and who pay no heed to His advice and admonitions.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 10, verses 101–103:

{101} Allah, exalted is He, calls His servants to look at what is in the heavens and the earth. What is meant by this is the looking of reflection, consideration, contemplation of what is in them and what they contain, and insight. Indeed, in that are signs for a people who believe, and lessons for a people who have certainty, indicating that Allah alone is the one worthy of worship, the praised, possessor of majesty and honour, and of the great names and attributes. ﴿But signs and warnings avail not a people who do not believe.﴾ For they do not benefit from the signs, due to their turning away and their obstinacy.

{102–103} ﴿Do they then await anything but the like of the days of those who passed away before them?﴾ That is: do these people who do not believe in the signs of Allah, after their clarity, await anything but the like of the days of those who passed away before them, i.e., of destruction and punishment? For they did as they did, and the way of Allah operates among the earlier and the later. ﴿Say: "Then wait, I am with you among those who wait."﴾ You will know to whom the good outcome and the salvation in this world and the Hereafter belong. And it belongs only to the messengers and their followers. Therefore He said: ﴿Then We save Our messengers and those who believe﴾ from the hardships of this world and the Hereafter and their severities. ﴿Thus it is an obligation upon Us, [that] We save the believers.﴾ We have made it binding upon Ourselves. Indeed, Allah defends those who believe; for according to the measure of faith the servant has, salvation from hardships is attained for him.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 10, verses 101–103:

{101} Allah, exalted is He, calls His servants to look at what is in the heavens and the earth. What is meant by this is the looking of reflection, consideration, contemplation of what is in them and what they contain, and insight. Indeed, in that are signs for a people who believe, and lessons for a people who have certainty, indicating that Allah alone is the one worthy of worship, the praised, possessor of majesty and honour, and of the great names and attributes. ﴿But signs and warnings avail not a people who do not believe.﴾ For they do not benefit from the signs, due to their turning away and their obstinacy.

{102–103} ﴿Do they then await anything but the like of the days of those who passed away before them?﴾ That is: do these people who do not believe in the signs of Allah, after their clarity, await anything but the like of the days of those who passed away before them, i.e., of destruction and punishment? For they did as they did, and the way of Allah operates among the earlier and the later. ﴿Say: "Then wait, I am with you among those who wait."﴾ You will know to whom the good outcome and the salvation in this world and the Hereafter belong. And it belongs only to the messengers and their followers. Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 10, verses 104–106:

{104} Allah the Exalted says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ), the leader of the messengers, the imam of the God-fearing, and the best of those who have certainty: {Say, "O mankind, if you are in doubt about my religion"}; that is, if you are in uncertainty and confusion. As for me, I am not in doubt about it. Rather, I have certain knowledge that it is the truth and that what you invoke besides Allah is falsehood, and I have clear proofs and brilliant evidence for this. Therefore He said: {then I do not worship those you worship besides Allah}, meaning the rivals, the idols, and others. This is because they neither create, nor provide sustenance, nor manage any affair; they are merely created and subjugated, and there is nothing in them that would call for their worship. {But I worship Allah, who causes you to die}; that is, He is Allah, who created you, who causes you to die, then resurrects you to recompense you for your deeds. He is the One who deserves to be worshipped, to be prayed to, [to be submitted to], and prostrated to. {And I have been commanded to be among the believers.}

{105} {And [I was commanded], "Direct your face toward the religion, inclining to truth"}; that is, make your outward and inward deeds sincerely for Allah, and establish all the laws of the religion. {Inclining} means turning toward Allah and turning away from everything else. {And never be among the polytheists}: neither in their condition, nor be with them.

{106} {And do not invoke, besides Allah, that which can neither benefit you nor harm you}: This is a description of every created being, that it neither benefits nor harms; the one who truly benefits and harms is Allah, the Exalted. {And if you do}; that is, if you invoke besides Allah that which neither benefits you nor harms you, {then indeed you would be, at that time, among the wrongdoers}; that is, those who harm themselves by destroying them. This wrongdoing is shirk, as Allah the Exalted said: {Indeed, shirk is a great wrongdoing.} So if the best of creation, were he to invoke another alongside Allah, would be among the wrongdoers and polytheists, then how about others?!

This wrongdoing is shirk, as Allah the Exalted said: {Indeed, shirk is a great wrongdoing.} So if the best of creation, were he to invoke another alongside Allah, would be among the wrongdoers and polytheists, then how about others?!

This is one of the greatest proofs that Allah alone deserves to be worshipped, for He is the One who benefits and harms, who gives and withholds. When harm befalls a person, such as poverty, sickness, or the like: {There is none to remove it except Him}, because if all creation gathered together to benefit someone with something, they would benefit him only with what Allah has written; and if they gathered together to harm anyone, they would not be able to inflict any of that harm unless Allah willed it. For this reason He said: {And if He touches you with good, then there is no repeller of His bounty}; that is, none of creation can repel His bounty and kindness, just as He said, Exalted is He: {Whatever Allah grants to people of mercy, none can withhold it; and whatever He withholds, none can release after Him} [Qur'an 35:2]. {He causes it to reach whom He wills of His servants}; that is, He singles out with His mercy whomever He wills of His creation, and Allah is the Possessor of great bounty. {And He is the Oft-Forgiving}: for all lapses, who guides His servant to the means of His forgiveness; then, when the servant does them, Allah forgives his sins, major and minor. {The Most Merciful}: whose mercy encompasses everything and whose generosity reaches all that exists, such that no existent can do without His kindness for the blink of an eye.

When the servant knows, by conclusive proof, that Allah alone is the One who bestows blessings, removes calamities, gives good deeds, and removes evil deeds and distresses, and that no one among creation has any of this in his hand except what Allah causes to take place through him, he is certain that Allah is the Truth and that what they invoke besides Him is falsehood. For this reason, when He had made the clear proof manifest, He said after it:

{108} Say, [O Messenger], once the proof has become clear: "O mankind, the truth has come to you from your Lord" — that is, the true report, confirmed by proofs, about which there is no doubt in any respect, and it has reached you from your Lord. Among the greatest of His nurturing of you is that He sent down to you this Qur'an, in which there is an explanation of everything, and which contains every kind of ruling, divine guidance, and praiseworthy moral conduct, which is the greatest nurturing of you and the greatest benevolence from Him toward you. Thus right guidance has been distinguished from error, and no one has any excuse left. "Whoever is guided" by God's guidance — by knowing the truth, understanding it, and preferring it over other things — "is guided only for his own self." God, the Exalted, is free of need from His servants, and the fruit of their deeds returns only to them. "And whoever goes astray" from guidance — by turning away from knowledge of the truth or from acting upon it — "then he goes astray only to his own loss," for he does not harm God in any way; he harms only himself. "And I am not over you a guardian," who preserves your deeds and calls you to account for them. I am only a clear warner to you, and God is your Guardian. So look to your own souls while you are within the period of respite.

{109} "And follow" [O Messenger] what is revealed to you — in knowledge, action, state, and calling others to it. "And be patient" in that, for this is the highest kind of patience, and its outcome is praiseworthy. So do not be lazy or impatient; rather, persist and remain steadfast "until God judges" between you and those who denied you. "And He is the best of judges," for His judgment is founded on perfect justice and equity, for which He is praised. The Messenger, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, complied with his Lord's command and remained firm upon the straight path, until God made His religion prevail over all other religions and gave him victory over his enemies by the sword and the spear, after God had already granted him victory over them through argument and proof. So to God belongs all praise and fine commendation, as befits His majesty, His greatness, His perfection, and the vastness of His benevolence.

The commentary on Surah Yunus is complete. And praise be to God, Lord of the worlds.
